children.translated_text: Of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance,
with the collyrium-stick of knowledge,
whose eyes were opened —
to that glorious <s>Guru</s>, I bow.
With shoulders like a lion's, with cheeks most sweetly smiling,
displaying inconceivable, brilliant, <s>rasa</s>-filled (aesthetic sentiment), wondrous, manifold transformations,
bearing a radiance delightful as the interior of a fully-bloomed golden lotus —

children.text: ekībhūtam vapur avatu vo rādhayā mādhavasya
children.translated_text: may the form of <s>Mādhava</s> united with <s>Rādhā</s> protect you!
The cluster of soft, reddish finger-petals, reddened by the pollen
in the form of saffron powder from the bud-breasts of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>,
with filament-networks of rays from the nails [shining with] the honey of devotees' faith —
may the lotus-foot, with its calf as stem, of the enemy of <s>Pūtanā</s> protect us!
In the ocean of <s>bhakti-rasa</s> (devotional aesthetic sentiment),
those who move about, having overcome the fear of Time's net,
the devotee-<s>makaras</s> (crocodiles) who have not resorted to
the river of <s>mukti</s> (liberation) — I bow to them.
At dawn, at the house of <s>Śrīvāsa</s>, awakened by the sounds of the twice-born,
resembling Vedic chanting, instantly freed from sleep and thrilled with horripilation,
experiencing the presence of <s>Rādhā</s> beside <s>Hari</s>, with tears flowing from the eyes,
the body bathed [in tears], golden like finest gold — O mind, worship [Him]!
At night's end, awakened by the many loud cries uttered by startled <s>Vṛndā</s>,

children.text: padyair hṛdyair ahṛdyair api sukha-śayanād utthitau tau sakhībhiḥ
children.translated_text: by the charming verses of parrots and <s>śārī</s>-birds — some pleasing, some not — risen from their happy bed,

children.text: dṛṣṭau hṛṣṭau tadātvodita-rati-lalitau kakkha ī-gīḥ saśaṅkau
children.translated_text: seen by their delighted <s>sakhīs</s>, those two displaying the beauty of love just arisen, apprehensive at the sound of laughter,

children.text: rādhā-kṛṣṇau satṛṣṇāv api nija-nija-dhāmny āpta-talpau smarāmi
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, still longing, yet [returning] to their respective abodes and beds — I remember them.
Awakened at their respective times of service,
the maidservants, devoted to their eternal practice,

children.text: nidraiva rātry antam avetya tā jahau
children.translated_text: sleep itself departed as it knew the end of night had come;
did it itself awaken [them]?
Rising from bed with startled eyes, for a moment
the unbroken private sleep of the two
sovereigns of love-sport —
perceiving it, the women sat in silence, with excessive wonder.
They asked one another, these women, with playful wit,
words filled with <s>rasa</s> (humor) and jest, with yawns,
their speech rolling with the dizziness of long wakefulness,
the rows of bee-like eyes licking each other's chests:
'Absorbed in thoughts of garlands and betel-leaf
befitting the late-night service' — then one said to the others:
'Overflowing with the fragrance and accessibility emanating
from the amorous youthful pair bound by <s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid), brimming with <s>rasa</s>,
do you know [the answer], O ones whose lotus-faces are on the net-path?
Sending forth your own glances into the interior of the chamber,
how does sleep embrace and satisfy
the lovers engaged in intense, exquisite dance-play?'
'The jewel-lamps placed here and there,
resembling unblossomed blue lotuses and <s>campakas</s> —
do these two [illumine them] with their own clusters of rays,
uncovered by ornaments, garlands, and garments?'
'That <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-cloud, surrounded by rows of steady and flickering [lightning-like women],
with excessively sweet <s>rasa</s> — did he perhaps
bathe [them], the women engaged in the duties of worship,
satisfying them with counter-worship from the very start?'
'With betel, garlands, various unguents,
and incense of charcoal, grain, and <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood),
being offered at appropriate times —
how many moments did they [the maidservants] spend thus?'
The breeze, to delight the king and queen of the bower,
shone forth with joy at that time;
I think, having awakened, [the breeze], with loose and feeble limbs,
was unable to travel swiftly.
The trees and creepers that blossomed at that very time —
kissing the ten directions with their loads of fragrance,
spread forth, entering the pathways of breath —
he [the breeze] awakened the rows of bees.
By their buzzing, sweet-sounding and intensely melodious,
<s>Vṛndā</s> then awoke and looked all around;
for the awakening of her two masters, she employed
the birds, with her knowledge of time, swiftly — this [<s>Vṛndā</s>].
For whose sake the best of twice-born [birds]
were first silent, though eager in mind for service —
receiving that command of <s>Vṛndā</s>, with delight
they sang all around the pleasure-bower.
Then the swarm of bees, greedy for nectar,
like the auspicious conch of <s>Ratīśa</s> (Kāmadeva),
in the beautiful bower of blossoming creepers,
hummed upon clusters of lotuses used as beds.
'She makes the humming sound
like a <s>jhallarī</s> (drum) of love's auspicious [rite] — to awaken <s>Govinda</s>,
intoxicated with honey,
the row of bees swells with delight.'
'The row of <s>pika</s>-birds (cuckoos), like the <s>vīṇā</s> of <s>Manoja</s> (Kāmadeva),
distinctly sounding the fifth note,
sang in a high pitch,
"<s>kuhū</s>, <s>kuhū</s>" again and again.'
'Bearing the melody-pattern of love's sweet <s>vipañcī</s> (lute),
seated beside her beloved, cooing with the intoxication of passion,
her throat made clear by tasting clusters of tender buds,
the row of female cuckoos makes the <s>kākalī</s> (soft melodious sound) upon the mango tree.'
'Driving away the deer of modesty, religious observance,
and shame of the <s>gopīs</s> — into the wolves of pride, wrathfully,
under the pretext of the pigeon's cooing, I think,
this king of the passion-hyenas roars.'
'In the matter of upholding the mountain of <s>Rādhā's</s> composure, who else is capable without
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>? And for subduing the maddened black elephant [of passion] — are chains [sufficient]?

children.text: anyāḥ kā vṛṣabhānu-jām iha vinā dhanyām atīvādṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Who other than the blessed daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> is so honored here?

children.text: kekāḥ kiṃ samudīrayanti śikhinas tau bodhayantaḥ prage
children.translated_text: What cries do the peacocks raise, awakening those two at dawn?'
'With short, long, and protracted [vowels] combined —
"ku-kūkū-kū" — that sound
the rooster too uttered at dawn,
like a young Brahmin student practicing the <s>Vedas</s>.'
Then, though awakened by the clamor of the birds,
those two, their wakefulness unknown to each other,
anxious at the breaking of their tight embrace,
remained with eyes closed by some pretense.
That wise parrot, knower of <s>Vṛndā's</s> gestures,
like <s>Śuka</s> (Śukadeva), skilled in the meaning of the <s>Bhāgavata</s>,
expert in awakening, being the supreme
abode of love for the Lord of the worlds — he spoke:
'Victory to You, O nectar for the eyes of the <s>gopī</s>-folk
who are expert in all arts of <s>Smara's</s> (Cupid's) amorous play!
O elephant of the river of love of Your beloved!
O You who flood the worlds with Your own sweetness!
You are immersed in the bliss of tasting Your beloved's lips —
that You do not awaken is not fitting, O ocean of <s>rasa</s>!
Your desire to play ceases only when You have ceased to desire,
and now this night is passing moment by moment.
Abandon sleep! Loosen Your embrace!
O Lord! Be ready to depart for <s>Vraja</s>!
Morning has come — follow Your own cleverness,
conceal Your amorous nature and make it fearsome [to others].'
'Victory, O delight of <s>Vraja</s>! O <s>Nanda's</s>
moon-ray upon the ocean of the heart! O Lord!
O blossom of the meritorious creeper of the queen of <s>Goṣṭha</s>!
Proceed to Your home and delight Your kinsmen!'
'O friend of <s>Gokula</s>! Victory! O ocean of <s>rasa</s>!
Awaken! Leave the bed, O moon-like one!
The one favorable to Your love, who has taken refuge at the base of Your arms —
awaken Your beloved, weary from the weight of love-sport!'
'This dawn is rising, reddening swiftly;
by nature compassionate to the host of young women,
O Lord of <s>Vraja</s>! Secretly go to Your abode,
quickly, to the bank of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (Yamunā)!'
The auspicious <s>śārī</s>-bird then spoke, subtle in intellect,
like a <s>śārī</s> (die) established in a position approved in [the game of] dice:
'Victory, O Queen! O chief among young women whose beauty and
fortune of amorous play causes longing in <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) herself!'
'O lotus-faced one! You who are deeply languid-limbed from the exertion of love-play —

children.text: svapiṣi sakhi! niśānte yat tavāyaṃ na doṣaḥ
children.translated_text: you sleep, O friend! At night's end, this is no fault of yours;

children.text: dig iyam aruṇitaindrī kintu paśyāvir āsīt
children.translated_text: but look! This eastern direction has become reddened —
she appeared, O virtuous one, like the moon's friend, unable to bear your happiness!'
'You who now recline, intoxicated by drinking the honey
of the lotus-face of your <s>rati-vallabha</s> (lord of love) —
that is inappropriate now; rather, it is now proper
for me to awaken you at dawn.'
'<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> too is sleepless, embraced by His beloved;
the beloved too is sleepless, embraced by Him;
yet from the bed, though disturbed by dawn,
this couple was unable to rise at all.'
'Her beautiful hips positioned upon <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> knees,
her breasts placed on His chest, her face pressed to His face,
her arms placed around His neck, His arm as her pillow —

children.text: kāntā na hīṅgati manāg api labdha-bodhā
children.translated_text: the beloved does not stir even slightly, though awakened.'
Skilled in composing the <s>līlā</s> (pastimes) of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>,
his wings spread wide with the bliss of love for Him,
the parrot named <s>Dakṣa</s>, perched in the bower's thicket,
spoke — he who had trained a multitude of parrots:
'The <s>cakravākī</s> (ruddy goose) casts one eye toward the east

children.text: cakṣuḥ kānte tvaritam aparaṃ dūrage cakravākī
children.translated_text: where the dawn's rays are spreading, and the other swiftly toward her distant beloved;
the owls, seized by fear, entering tree-hollows, become silent;

children.text: śaṅke bhāsvān udayam udagāt kṛṣṇa! nidrāṃ jahīhi
children.translated_text: I suspect the sun has risen — O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! Abandon sleep!'
'Victory, victory, O ocean of virtues! O life-bond of Your beloved!
O sun to the lotuses of <s>Vraja</s>! O jewel-crest of noble arts!

children.text: iha hi rajanī-śeṣe kiṃ manā nātha! śeṣe
children.translated_text: Here at night's end, with what mind do You remain, O Lord?
Even recognizing the time, will the bower-bed [hold You longer]?

children.text: ayam api ca śikhaṇḍī jāgaritvaiva khaṇḍī
children.translated_text: This peacock too, having awakened, breaking [the silence],
uttering beautiful cries, discerning time's end —
languishes for the removal of Your sleep, impoverished of mastery;

children.text: śiva śiva nija-sevā-kālam ujjhanti ke vā?
children.translated_text: auspicious, auspicious! Who indeed abandons their own time of service?'
'Having learned the art from <s>Vṛndā's</s> mouth,
the <s>śārī</s>-bird, captivating with many verses,
intoxicated with the honey of growing affection for <s>Rādhā</s>,
is intent upon dispelling Her sleep:'
'Abandon sleep! Leave the bower-bed!
Go to your home, O friend! Do not be slothful!

children.text: kāntaṃ ca bodhaya na bodhaya loka-lajjāṃ
children.translated_text: Awaken your beloved, but do not awaken public shame —
for the wise elevate timely action.'
'Resting on the lap of <s>Vraja's</s> lord's son, free from anxiety,
O moon-faced one! Why do you linger deeply at night's end?
O host of joy-bees! Do not remain long in the bower —

children.text: na gaṇayasi vigarhāṃ kiṃ guruṇām anarhām?
children.translated_text: do you not consider the undeserved censure of the elders?'
'O beautiful-toothed one! The swarms of intoxicated bees,
hiding in the laps of night-lotuses, become restless when the time comes,
and move toward the radiance of day-lotuses, undepressed —
time itself is the lord of grief and joy.'
'The sky with very faint stars, your body with its necklace scattered,
the forms of <s>śephālikā</s> (night-jasmine) flowers fallen —
these three now appear of one form, though at that time [different];

children.text: api yad api tathāpi tvad-vapuḥ śrībhir āpi
children.translated_text: yet even so, your body surpasses them in beauty.'
'Like your scattered necklace of broken, fallen pearls,
this host of stars has become diminished, with only a small remainder;
seeing your long sleep, <s>Arundhatī</s> is embarrassed;
look at the constellation of the Seven Sages, encircling [you] as if embracing!'
Hearing the exceedingly charming, ear-delighting
utterances of those melodious <s>śārikā</s>-birds and parrots,
<s>Rādhā</s> awoke, Her sleep-sloth broken,
and that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> too, His desire for sleep-play exhausted.
Simultaneously, both their sleep shattered, their composure destroyed;
simultaneously, the play of both their sidelong glances — wondrous;
simultaneously, both filled with distress born of rolling [dizzily];
the absence of seeing each other [clearly] brought sorrow.
With softly jingling bangles and anklets,
the radiance of their limbs surging greatly,
with the tips of disheveled locks rising and wrapping,
the face illuminated by the splendor of the necklace upon the chest,
with the flurry of searching for fallen garments,
beautiful with lotus-hands placed here and there —
the rising from the bed of those two sportive lovers —
he [the poet] gathered that [vision] as if it were the wealth of the three worlds.
With eyes rolling and languid, all limbs loose,
hair disheveled — that pair of <s>rasikas</s> (connoisseurs of love),
sitting bent, somehow in their stumbling
took support of one another.
Raising both arms with interlocked tender fingers,
preceded by the onset of a yawn, stretching the body,
with closing eyes, face pained by the nail-marks revealed on her breasts,

children.text: nā-nā-neti punar nakha-kṣata-dhiyā sā kṛṣṇa-pāṇī dadhe
children.translated_text: [saying] 'no, no!' — then, thinking [the marks were from] nails, she took <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> hands [in hers].
Covering with a thin edge of cloth her lotus-face
bathed by the moonlight of her emerging row of teeth, drawn by her right hand,
with neck gracefully tilted in playful <s>līlā</s>, with soft sounds of the flicking
of the left hand's fingers accompanied by the sound of moving bangles — <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> yawned.
Languidly lifting the head upward toward the neck,
this [arm] entwined around each other, hands clasped together —
moving with the swaying triple-bend posture,

children.text: paridhir iva mukhendor bhāti dordvandvam asyāḥ
children.translated_text: the pair of her arms shines like a halo around her moon-like face.
Then the Lord, having risen, seated himself on the bed,
pretending sleep, with closed eyes,
drawing his weary beloved onto his lap with both arms,
he gazes at her sweetness, saying 'How beautiful!'
With eyes rolling like <s>khañjarīṭa</s> (wagtail) birds,
with a swarm of bee-like curls playfully swaying on her forehead,
the face of his beloved, resembling a morning lotus,
<s>Acyuta</s> drank with his eyes, [her face] slightly smiling.
With the pair of arms, all fingers intertwined,
churning [and] embracing her body,
radiant with the beauty of teeth revealed by a full yawn,
<s>Mukunda</s> rejoiced upon beholding his beloved.
At that very moment, did the rays of radiance from her teeth, revealed by yawning,
perform an <s>āratī</s> (waving of lights) with ruby lamps?
The beauty of her half-opened, drowsy eye-corners,
being licked by each other with the connoisseurship of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic delight).
At dawn, [seeing her] sleeping supine on his lap, softly feigning tears with a slight smile on her face,
her hair half-loosened at the tips, wearing a garland of crushed flowers, her necklace broken,
opening and closing her rolling, languid pair of eyes, eager to behold her own beloved's face,

children.text: kāntāṃ tāṃ keli-tāntāṃ mudam atulatamām āpa paśyan vrajenduḥ
children.translated_text: seeing that beloved, wearied by love-play, the moon of <s>Vraja</s> attained the most incomparable joy.
Of her whose limbs were [beautiful as] golden lotuses, rendered languid by the exertion of intense love-making,
whose body rested on her lover's lap, beautiful as fresh <s>tāmāla</s> (dark tamāla tree),
if <s>Campā</s> (the golden champak vine) trembling upon a fresh rain-cloud were to stand still,

children.text: śrī-rādhāyāḥ sphuṭam iha tadā sāmya-kakṣām avāpsyat
children.translated_text: then indeed it would clearly attain equality with <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> here.
With sparkling <s>makara</s> (crocodile-shaped) earrings, with the rise of a sweet gentle smile,
with eyes languid from intoxication, fragrant as a lotus, with playfully swaying curls,
seeing <s>Hari's</s> face, its lip-beauty marred by her own tooth-marks and smudged with <s>añjana</s> (collyrium),
the lotus-eyed one again became eager for amorous play.
Shyness born of mutual gazing,
eyes slightly contracted with trembling bashfulness,
seeing the slightly smiling face of his beloved,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, his desire inflamed, was [aroused] again.
Lifting her head from below with his left hand,
and [touching] her chin with the other,
with neck bent, [he kissed] her cheek beautiful with a smile —
he kissed the face of his beloved again and again.
Submerged in the ocean of bliss from touching her beloved's lips,
shaking her hand, her eyes slightly contracted,
'Don't! Don't!' — with faint syllables, her voice choked,
she spread delight to the eyes of her <s>sakhīs</s> (girlfriends).
'The nectar of beauty, unique in the three worlds, that is mine,
and this limitlessly sweet youth —
today indeed it has attained its full fruition in every way,
for my beloved has enjoyed it most completely with joy.'
Having reflected thus for a moment, she who had drunk all sweetness through his eyes
spoke to her beloved,
her inner joy exceedingly radiant at the corners of her eyes,
her lotus-face a pleasure-ground for the goddess <s>Lakṣmī</s>:

children.text: bho bho vilāsinn avadhehi yat tvayā
children.translated_text: 'O, O playful one! Consider that by you
I have been made [disheveled], with ornaments and garments loosened.
Before my friends come looking for me in the morning,

children.text: drutaṃ samādhitsasi tan na kiṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: will you not quickly set things right again?'
'Exercise your cleverness — adorn me,
and propitiate <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love), the cherished deity,
who dwells in the temple of our minds — [he] whom you
have expelled outward by these very marks [of love].'
'You speak truly — the body-born (<s>Anaṅga</s>, Kāmadeva) is indeed [our] cherished deity;
manifesting upon the altar of your body,
I worship him with ornaments, garments, fragrances, and flowers,
with garlands, sandalwood paste, and the rest' — thus he spoke to her.
Having heard the words
of the sovereign lady, skilled in service,
eager to offer
the articles suitable for that [adorning],
opening the door quietly, without noise,
graceful with particularly gentle footsteps,
having ascertained that those two were awake, the row of maidservants
entered the dwelling fearlessly.
Here and there, with placed jewel-lamps,
resembling unopened blue lotuses and <s>campaka</s> flowers,
those two bestowed with their own clusters of rays,
uncovered by ornaments, garlands, and garments,
with lips bitten by each other's teeth, languid from love-play,
bodies marked by nail-scratches, the beauty of decorative leaf-designs effaced,
garments loosened, beautiful locks [disheveled], necklaces and flower-garlands torn,

children.text: muhur mumudire puraḥ samabhilakṣya tāḥ sva-priyau
children.translated_text: those [maidservants] rejoiced again and again upon beholding their two beloveds before them.
Then, as he slowly, slowly drew the comb
placed in the hand of <s>Bhānumatī</s>,
he arranged her tresses — he who was expert in braiding
hair adorned with <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) garlands.
With liquids of musk, sandalwood, and saffron,
blended with a love-letter [design],
he, holding a fresh brush, made beautiful, wonderful paintings
adorned with garland designs [on her body].
With a pair of <s>aṅka</s> (decorative marks), beautified with novel radiance from clove-blossoms,
that beautiful one,
adorned her ears; and with fresh <s>añjana</s> (collyrium)
he anointed those lotus-like eyes of hers.
When he placed a necklace glittering with clusters of radiance,
his beloved spoke with love-intoxicated boldness:
'The sandalwood bodice that you tore —
on my breasts — won't you make amends for that from somewhere?'
'Those [friends] of yours, <s>Viśākhā</s> and the others, who pride themselves greatly
in the art of painting —
I shall astonish them today with wonderful, extraordinary

children.text: citrair vicitrair iti tāṃ jagāda saḥ
children.translated_text: paintings made on your pair of breasts' — thus he told her.
Eager to offer articles for adornment,
<s>Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī</s>, <s>Līlā Mañjarī</s>, <s>Rati Mañjarī</s> and others [came forward],
as <s>Hari</s> was painting on her pair of breasts with a brush,
[he] became a target of the five arrows of <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the god of love).
And if his hand, trembling, [while painting] the curved line upon her breast,
repeatedly smudged the design with his chest —
I think he was fanning the fire of <s>Smara</s> (desire),
the clever one, intending to burn her composure as fuel.
<s>Kāma</s> (desire), having instantly rendered that one powerless with no small might,
fixing him in an uncontrolled state,
wiping, applying, breaking apart piece by piece,
with that very [material], he adorned both of them joyfully.
And those maidservants, with blossoming eyes, had long desired
that very embodiment of fulfilled purpose;
again desiring to make love, those two having come together,
all [maidservants] were driven out on some pretext.
Again, from the deep, whirling union of their beautiful faces,
resplendent with the desired embrace of steady vine-like arms,

children.text: kṣaṇam api dara-suptyā śaṃ bhajāvetya tas tāv
children.translated_text: 'Rest for a moment with light slumber for peace!' — [saying] thus, those two
on the crooked flower-bed became [figures with] loosened limbs.
What [use was] that bed, tormented by [previous] separation?
Or what [use] of that sleep, barely obtained along with an embrace?

children.text: uṣasi na ca vihātuṃ hanta śaktau khagās tau
children.translated_text: Alas! In the morning, unable even to depart, those two birds —
yet [other] birds, separated from them, sang out to those two.
'Disregard the family conventions — do not sleep in the bower!
Abandon the sleep that destroys love-making — arise quickly!
See, the night has especially ended with only a remnant of darkness remaining;
do not cause obstruction to the group of kinsmen who have lost composure!'

children.text: iyam ajani digaindrī dṛśyatāṃ devi! sāndrī-
children.translated_text: 'This eastern quarter has appeared — behold, O goddess!
A stream of intensifying redness, imitating your lotus-feet,

children.text: iyam api ca varākī satvarā cakravākī
children.translated_text: and this poor <s>cakravākī</s> (ruddy goose), hastening
to her mate (<s>rathāṅga</s>), now that the separation-sorrow is broken —'
'Also, wishing to attain the beauty of your face, with excessive greed,
his desires unfulfilled, wishing to abandon his own body,
having reached the peak of the western mountain, see how high —

children.text: vrajati śaśadharo 'staṃ vārayed adya kas tam
children.translated_text: the moon sets — who could restrain him today?'
'O beautiful-faced one! Release the seal of sleep from your eyes, shaking off drowsiness;
display the radiance of your face, [bright] as flashing lightning!
With ornaments loosened from love-play, attire scattered and disarranged,
with disheveled body — let these [friends] attend upon you, gathered together!'
'Look! This one, nourished by your own hand, has entered
your presence — O moon-faced one! — a graceful-limbed doe;
cast a slightly rippling sidelong glance upon her,

children.text: bhavatu bata kṛtārthā prītaye te samarthā
children.translated_text: so that she may be fulfilled and capable of [bringing] you delight!'
'Thinking [your foot] a fresh sprout, from inner purity born of love,
to taste your reddish lotus-foot, O beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!
She quickly approaches, bearing for your <s>sakhīs</s> (friends)
the tribute of a blow from her lotus-[like] hoof — she who has arrived.'
'O moon-faced one! Playful in enjoying even a mere morsel of your leftover food,
attentive only to the fragrance of the water [that washed] your feet,
also grief-stricken from the absence of seeing you,
depending solely on the sight of the moon-disc of your face —'
'<s>Hari</s>, exceedingly curious, measures your pair of eyes,
to fathom the guileless love of her whose eyes [express it];
comparing [them] somehow with a string of pure pearls and eloquent speech,
he is certainly dispelling [his own] doubt.'
Thus spoke those <s>śārikās</s> (mynah birds), full of love,
words whose meanings were joy-giving, meant to awaken [the lovers];

children.text: yadi kim api viremuḥ patriṇas taṃ praṇemuḥ
children.translated_text: if they ceased at all, the other birds bowed to him,
having approached the bower, having attained an abundance of delight.
Then a flock of parrots, eager for <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> joy,
also awakened <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who was longing for the bed,
with their cooings, pleasing to the ear, gentle, delightful in sweet words and meaning,
most melodious, abundant, [sweet] as honey-wine.
Profound in the <s>rasa</s> (sentiment) of love, steady in beautiful words and meaning,
with softly sweet throats, unhesitating in love-talk,
some awakened [him] with discrimination of the proper time —

children.text: na khalu bata vidagdhāḥ kārya-kāle vimugdhāḥ
children.translated_text: truly, the clever ones are never bewildered at the time of duty!
'O fortunate one! As the remainder of the night lies beautifully in the house of sleep,

children.text: tvam iti hi jananī te saṃśayaṃ svaṃ dhunīte
children.translated_text: your mother shakes off her own doubt, [thinking] "He is [here]" —
then, knowing the [right] time, hastening for the purpose of waking [you],

children.text: svayam iyam upagantrī sneha evātra mantrī
children.translated_text: she herself will come — love alone is the counselor here.'
'You are a knower of the [right] time, the sole destroyer of all sorrows,
you are the friend of the world, an ocean of noble virtues;
the bed in the house of the devoted is an embodiment of the wish-fulfilling tree of joy —

children.text: yad api tad api muñca svasti te'smād udañca
children.translated_text: yet even that, release! Blessings upon you — rise from it!'
'The intoxicated young bees, the end of night having arrived,
having abandoned the interior of the flower-groves, have awoken from sleep;
they engage in some play in the lanes of lotuses —
when there is discernment of the proper time, who in the world is deluded?'
'Somewhere there is the sorrow of [parting] faces, somewhere the grace of laughter;

children.text: kva ca dayita-viyogaḥ kvāpi kāntasya yogaḥ
children.translated_text: somewhere the separation from the beloved, somewhere the union with the lover;
in the extreme dissimilarity between the night-lotus and day-lotus paths,
does not time become vast with the splendor of agitation?'

children.text: jaya subhaga! namas te śrūyatāṃ satvaras te
children.translated_text: 'Victory, O fortunate one! Salutations to you! Hear [this] quickly:
this red-crested rooster, pained by long lying [in wait],
swelling with the delight of the arrival of the time of his own service,
indeed, one skilled in timing is never bewildered at the time of duty!'
Then, having truly awakened, shaking their wings,
stretching their necks, the roosters crowed loudly;
when the roosters [crowed] five or six times at first,
<s>Rādhā</s> awoke then, distressed.
Considering those [roosters] as enemies of the special embrace with <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> body,

children.text: tān eva matveti śaśāpa sā ruṣā
children.translated_text: she cursed them angrily:
'O wretches! Go quickly to the city of the dead (<s>Pretapura</s>)!
Why do you crow there, you spur-footed ones?'
Separating slightly from her beloved's chest,
finding them suddenly silent,
embracing her lover again with light drowsiness,
she, being served [by sleep], shone forth once more.
Then from the lattice-window, the fish-like glances — their abode —
greatly followed the flood of [the lovers'] beauty;
[the maidservants] who purchase with billions of half-lives
even a particle of the ray of delight arising from the joy of those two.
<s>Viśākhā</s> said: 'Behold, dear friend! The lovers,
without garments, beautiful upon a heap of cloth,
sporting yet supremely captivating, with their own
limbs [appearing] bodiless, languid yet radiant —'
'Bestowing the ornament of love through play, themselves [like] <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless one),
free from cosmetics, yet mutually [beautiful as if] anointed with <s>añjana</s> (collyrium),
marked by the loosened color of [bitten] lips,
marked by the deep color of [passionate] attachment.'
Then <s>Lalitā</s> spoke: 'Let it be observed —
in this battle of love (<s>Smarāja</s>), on which of the two does victory rest?
Of these two, whose lips are bitten and whose heads are thrown back
by the pulling of hair, whose chests are scratched by nails —'
'Under the pretext of breast-<s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron paste), [<s>Kāma</s>] deposited
the love upon the lotus-feet of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>,
as long as he, with his red-tipped forelock, placed
that brilliant [mark] with his very head upon her feet.'
Thus, for a moment, those [maidservants] with unnoticed limbs,
in low voices describing those two,
Celebrating their own good fortune,
they were immersed in that great ocean of bliss.

children.text: tataḥ punas tān atha i ibhādī-
children.translated_text: Then again, [a bird] among [those perched on] the great trees,
cooing sweetly, spoke, having shaken off drowsiness:
'Ah! Grant me permission to sleep for just a moment,'

children.text: datteti sā mo ayad aṅgam īṣat
children.translated_text: she said, and slightly moved her limbs.
<s>Kādamba</s> ducks, geese, <s>sārasas</s> (cranes),
pigeons, <s>śārī</s> birds, parrots, peacocks, and cuckoos,
sang melodiously, roaming through the waters and lands of the pleasure-grove,
[their song] resembling the nectar of tales about <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Awakening simultaneously, the two lovers felt the pain
born of impending separation, from the languor of their limbs.
Those two, of the luster of <s>campaka</s> flowers and blue lotuses, [like] a bow,
and [found] delight in their breasts through a dense embrace.
Then her friends, with joyful smiling faces,
laughing and urging that <s>sakhī</s> (female friend) among themselves,
anxious from all sides about the dreadful dawn,
entered the bower filled with buzzing bees.
Seeing the <s>sakhīs</s> (friends), with laughing faces,
having approached nearby, with restless eyes,
giving doubled delight to the beloved,
she rose from the pair of thighs of her beloved.
Having risen hastily, concealing her body
with the yellow upper garment seized in haste,
<s>Rādhā</s> sat down beside her beloved,
bashfully gazing at the faces of those [friends].
Then, adorned with the congratulations of the affectionate friends,
the beauty of those two blossomed joyfully.
She herself, <s>Rūpa-mañjarī</s>, for the pair of amorous players,
was most expert in adorning [them] appropriately for the occasion.
One placed a cushion behind [their] backs;
another then covered them both with a soft cloth;
yet another, offering a nectarean drink to their mouths,
dispelled their dizziness and made their eyes bloom.
One, with a cloth slightly moistened with flower-water,
having wiped away the smeared collyrium, lac-dye, and the like,
brought the two faces to the [clarity of] a mirror,
so that each could see their own reflection — what [a sight]!
Another placed betel-leaf [preparations] in [the mouth of] the other;
one, with a jeweled lamp-stand,
quickly performed the auspicious <s>āratī</s> (lamp-waving ceremony) for them,
waving [the lamp] as if with the lights of her own life-breaths.
In the center, smeared with thick <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) paste from <s>Acyuta's</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>) body,
with both sides decorated with the lac-dye from <s>Rādhā's</s> feet,
variegated with drops of vermillion, sandalwood, and collyrium —
their bed revealed to the [friends] the nature of their love-play.
With its arrangement of crushed flower-heaps,
its surface painted with betel-stains and collyrium,
bearing the evident marks of the beloved's amorous sport —
the friends beheld the bed as if it were their own companion.
Here a smear of saffron paste, there a mark of vermillion,
as if the blood of the enemy — separation — were oozing from wounds, as an ally,
here a garland of flowers [looking like] a broken bow,
there a scattered necklace [looking like] a severed bowstring.
Here are marks of musk, there marks of collyrium,
resembling the broken tusks of the elephant of <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the god of love), shining forth.
That arena of love's battle, with waves of curiosity rising,
arose [as a spectacle] for the beautiful-faced friends who had arrived.
Showing His own chest to them,
<s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) spoke to them with a sidelong glance,
wishing to see the sweet variety of expressions
on the face of His beloved.
Seeing the beloved [moon] about to depart, as the moon [was setting],
fearful of separation at dawn, while the friends looked on,
as if wishing to see the painted canvas of the sky,
<s>Rādhā</s> drew a hundred crescent moons.

children.text: iti nigadati kṛṣṇe vīkṣya sāgre vayasyāḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> spoke thus, seeing the friends before her,
they, with laughing faces, with contracting, rolling eyes,
with blooming, spotless cheeks, with swaying, arched brows,
gazed at the beloved with sidelong glances, as if striking [him].
Closing with playful, jesting affection, deeply reddened at the corners with tears,
trembling with modesty, fear, and agitation, crooked with the weight of jealousy,
slightly smiling, with pupils blooming wide at the sight of the beloved's face —
<s>Rādhā's</s> glance spread the highest bliss upon the beloved's eyes.
Thus, while those two were immersed in the ocean of love's bliss,
the dawn-time sweetness of their amorous play,
having drunk it in, the friends, intoxicated with delight,
then forgot their duties appropriate to the occasion.
Seeing those two immersed in the ocean of amorous nectar,
and those friends blinded by the intoxication of love,
<s>Vṛndā</s>, anxious at the approach of dawn,
directed her <s>śārī</s> (myna bird), who understood her gestures.
Warding off the shame before elders, fear of the husband,
and the ridicule of the people,
the auspiciously-named <s>sārikā</s> (myna bird) spoke,
serving to awaken <s>Rādhikā</s>:

children.text: āgantā grāhayitvā tava patir adhunā goṣṭhataḥ kṣīra-bhārān
children.translated_text: 'Your husband, having sent the loads of milk from the cowshed, is about to come;

children.text: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha rādhe tad iha kuru gṛhe maṅgalāṃ vāstu-pūjāma
children.translated_text: arise, arise, O <s>Rādhā</s>! Perform the auspicious household worship here at home.

children.text: itthaṃ yāvad dhavāmbā tava nahi śayanād utthitā vāvadīti
children.translated_text: In the meanwhile, until your mother-in-law has not yet risen from her bed,

children.text: tāvac chayyā-niketaṃ vraja sakhi nibhṛtaṃ kuñjataḥ kañja-netre!!
children.translated_text: go secretly from this bower to your bedchamber, O lotus-eyed one!'
'Her mother-in-law, whose heart is muddied with suspicion, suspects her;
her husband, extremely harsh, true to his name <s>Abhimanyu</s>, searches for flaws;

children.text: ruṣṭābhīkṣṇaṃ parivadati sā hā nanandāpi mandā
children.translated_text: her constantly angry sister-in-law too speaks ill — alas, the wretched one!

children.text: prātar-jātaṃ tad api saralāṃ kṛṣṇa naināṃ jahāsi
children.translated_text: Even so, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, born at dawn, You do not abandon this innocent one.'
Her heart, an ocean of milk, churned by the fall
of the <s>Mandara</s> mountain of the <s>śārī</s> bird's words —
with the fresh fish of her darting eyes —
she, wretched with impending separation, arose from the bed.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> too, gazing at the beautiful face of the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>,
with eyes trembling with apprehension,
grasping the dark, fine garment of His beloved,
hastily rose from His bed.
Having exchanged their garments,
the two, now apprehensive,
holding each other's hands,
emerged from the bower.
Holding <s>Rādhā's</s> hand in His left hand and the flute
in His right, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
shone as He came out of the bowers, just as
a cloud embraced by a garland of lightning.

children.text: haimaṃ bhṛṅgāram ekā vyajanam atha parā svarṇa-daṇḍaṃ dadhānā
children.translated_text: One carrying a golden pitcher, another a fan, yet another holding a golden-handled mirror, another [carrying] a wondrous unguent of saffron and sandalwood,

children.text: kāpy ādarśaṃ sudarśaṃ ghusṛṇa-malayajā'matram anyā vicitram
children.translated_text: one a beautiful mirror, another varied [cosmetics],

children.text: kācit tāmbūla-pātraṃ maṇi-citam aparā sārikāṃ pañjarasthām
children.translated_text: one a jewel-studded betel-box, another a caged <s>sārikā</s> bird —

children.text: itthaṃ sakhyaḥ kiyat yāḥ pramudita-hṛdayā niryayuḥ kuñja-gehāt
children.translated_text: thus, several friends, with delighted hearts, came out of the bower-house.
Another, carrying the sapphire-and-gold canopy
of <s>Indra's</s> beloved, of ivory, with a vermillion-box,
resembling the lotus-bud on the breast of one with child,
came out of the bower with a gentle smile.
From the necklace whose string had been broken in the embrace,
gathering the scattered pearls joyfully,
one, tying them firmly in the hem of her garment,
came out of the bower-house.
Taking the ear-ornament that had fallen loose during love-play
hastily from the bed,
having come out, <s>Rati-mañjarī</s>
placed it on her mistress's ear.
Taking the bodice from the edge of the bed,
<s>Rūpa-mañjarī</s>,
the intimate confidante (<s>priyanarma-sakhī</s>), having come out,
secretly gave it to her friend.
Taking up a hair-ornament,
the maidservant <s>Guṇa-mañjarī</s>,
distributing chewed betel to them all,
went outside.
<s>Mañjulālī</s>, [taking] the garlands and ointments
that had fallen from the bodies of those two
and from the bed, giving [them]
to all, came outside.
Seeing before them the beloved one, his body wrapped in a dark-cloud [colored] garment,
and that friend, her body wrapped in yellow cloth, delighted,
those friends, laughing with mouths covered by their hands, in every direction,
exchanging crooked, darting glances with one another, rejoiced greatly.
Observing the playful teasing of those [friends],
the two, with wide-open eyes fixed on each other's faces,
immersed in the rising ocean of love's bliss,
became as if figures painted on a canvas.
The dark silk garment clinging to the beloved's body —

children.text: kṣamā nāsīt kāntā svam api paricetuṃ ghana-rucau
children.translated_text: the beloved was unable to perceive even her own [body] in that dark-hued [one];

children.text: svam ajñāsīt sphītaṃ harir api na pītaṃ priyatamā-
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> too did not recognize his own [garment] — the yellow [cloth] clinging

children.text: tanau līnaṃ cīnaṃ kanaka-ruci kambāv iva payaḥ
children.translated_text: to the beloved's body of golden luster, as if milk [merging] into gold.
Filled with impatience at the obstacle
to the drinking of the nectar of their love-play,
cursing the rising dawn,
then <s>Lalitā</s> spoke to her friend:
'Look, O <s>Rādhā</s>, at dawn this reddish one, the sinful rogue,
who, with his rays, disrupts the love-play of noble brides and their lovers —
though he has lost both his feet, even today he does not abandon us;
truly, as the saying goes, one's own nature is hard to give up.'
Casting a reddened glance upon the reddening dawn,
reddened with anger at the disruption of love-play,
with a smiling face born of <s>Lalitā's</s> jest,
the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) spoke, the gentle sweet-speaking one:
'Though footless, setting in half a moment,
crossing the sky, he rises again —

children.text: cet sorum enaṃ sa vidhir vyadhāsyad
children.translated_text: if the Creator had made him with feet,
there would not even be a rumor of night!'
Seeing the enchanting beauty of the dawn,
and having drunk in the nectar of her words,
<s>Mukunda</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), mind overflowing with joy, forgetting the journey to the cowshed,
spoke to her, the mistress of his life:
'Seeing this sun approaching at dawn,
like a lover who has enjoyed another's beloved —
behold, his body stained with the taint of consorting with the other direction (the west) —
this eastern [sky] has become as if reddened with jealousy!'
'See, O intoxicated one! Even the lord of the twice-born (the moon), though he destroys the darkness of all people, is himself subdued;

children.text: kānto 'yaṃ te samantāt sapadi nipatito vāruṇīṃ saṃniṣevya
children.translated_text: this lover of yours, having fallen everywhere at once after indulging in drink (<s>Vāruṇī</s>),
thus, embarrassed by the laughter of the lotuses that rejoiced at the contact with the sun —

children.text: śaṅke vaktraṃ pidhatte hy uṣasi kumudinī saṅkucadbhir dalaiḥ svaiḥ
children.translated_text: I suspect the night-lotus covers her face at dawn with her own contracting petals!'
'Seeing the destruction of darkness, these [owls], nourished by the moon,
resembling masses of darkness at night, are frightened at dawn;
[seeing] their friend (darkness), roaming by means of darkness, as one sheltered by it,
being devoured — "Alas, alas!" (kuhū, kuhū) — they call out with their own cries.'
The [female] peacock, filled with bliss from the company
of her beloved spring,
under the pretext of cooing,
seems to whistle with intoxication.
'See — the restless black bee follows
the female bee, tawny from sporting among the night-lotus families,
who had spent the night in the cup of a day-lotus,
O moon-faced one! [She is] making her bow of modesty.'
'Suspecting her beloved to be arriving,
doubly reddened by the reddish rays [of dawn],
the <s>cakravākī</s> (ruddy goose) kisses the <s>cakravāka</s> (her mate, the red lotus)
with her beak, overwhelmed with bliss.'
'O <s>Kalakaṇṭhī</s> (sweet-throated one)! The swan named <s>Kalasvana</s> (sweet-voiced),
seeing us, his wings spread wide with great delight,
though wishing to sport, abandoning his mate,

children.text: ta aṃ ta inyāḥ purataḥ sameti
children.translated_text: approaches before [us], to the [lake of] his beloved.'
'See, the intoxicated, melodious-throated female goose,
carrying in her beak the lotus-root released and enjoyed by her companion —
follows her mate, her eyes fixed on your lotus-face;
O lotus-faced one! That female goose is called <s>Tuṇḍiketī</s> by name.'
'A breeze roaming the peaks of <s>Malaya</s>, bearing the fragrance of lotuses,
empowered to teach the dance-art to the maidens of the creeper-city,
traveling over the waters, dispelling weariness,
it removes the network of perspiration of the noble beloved women and their lovers.'
Thus, while those two supreme ones engaged in the sweetest speech and amorous play,
seeing that he had forgotten the journey to his own home,
and those friends, beautiful with smiles, intoxicated with delight,
<s>Vṛndā</s>, the mistress of the forest, anxious because of the advancing day, [spoke] eagerly:
'The beautiful-faced women have risen, their moon-like faces blooming;
the night has departed, its moonlight extinguished.
Whether there be a disruption of love-play or not —
let the heart [decide] for a moment' — thus she reflected.
'As the darkness vanished progressively,
and the light increased accordingly,
so too she experienced only the pain in her heart;
even the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas) do not know the ways of <s>Vraja</s>.'
Then, understanding <s>Vṛndā's</s> gestures,
knowing the [right] time, perched in the tree,
the old female monkey illuminated
a verse:
'Clad in red garments, venerable to the good,
the morning <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight), an ascetic woman,
with the rays of the sun spreading upward
as her matted locks — she has arrived!'
Hearing the three syllables 'Ja-ṭi-lā' ('matted-haired') [uttered] by those [birds],
paleness was instantly assumed [by the lovers] —
rising from the jewel-mine of love-play,
fear alone cupped [them in its hands].
Fearful on the path of the slanderous-minded elders,
casting restless, trembling, agitated sidelong glances,
profoundly virtuous, steadfast in the battle of love,
<s>Rādhikā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s> departed, free from the weariness of love.

children.text: na pathi na bhavane vā lakṣitau tau vane vā
children.translated_text: Not noticed on the road, nor at home, nor in the forest,
by their innate, genuine love, by their own power of bliss,
creating a festival for the eyes of their attendants,
then, sporting on the path, the two who enchant the world shone forth.
lifting the garlands slipping from their hair and loosening garments,
the two, frightened, hastening separately on the dense path —
seeing those two trembling with fear, by the name '<s>Jaṭilā</s>' (the matted-haired one),

children.text: sakhyas tatas tata itaś cakitā nirīyuḥ
children.translated_text: the friends then rushed out in alarm from here and there.
On the left, the attendants of <s>Candrāvalī</s>, the elders of the cowherd settlement ahead,

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ paścāt ku ila-jaṭilām āgatāṃ manyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, thinking that the crooked <s>Jaṭilā</s> had come from behind,

children.text: yāntīṃ kāntāṃ sabhaya-caṭulāṃ dakṣiṇe draṣṭum utkaś
children.translated_text: eager to see his beloved going to the right, fearful and restless,

children.text: cañcad-grīvaṃ diśi diśi dṛśau prerayan goṣṭham āyāt
children.translated_text: turning his neck this way and that, casting his eyes in every direction, came to the cowherd settlement.

children.text: mlānām utkṣipya mālāṃ tru ita-maṇisaraḥ kajjalaṃ vibhrad oṣṭhe
children.translated_text: Lifting up his wilted garland, his jeweled necklace broken, bearing <s>kajjala</s> (collyrium) on his lips,

children.text: saṃkīrṇāṅgo nakhāṅkair diśi diśi vikiran ghūrṇite netra-padme
children.translated_text: his body covered with nail-marks, scattering [glances] in every direction, his lotus-eyes rolling,

children.text: paśya mlānāṅga-yaṣṭiḥ sphuṭam aparicito gopa-goṣṭhībhir agre
children.translated_text: see — with wilted limbs, clearly unrecognized by the <s>gopī</s> assemblies before him,

children.text: goṣṭhe goṣṭhendra-sūnuḥ praviśati rajanau dhvaṃsam āsādayantyām
children.translated_text: the son of the lord of the cowherds enters the settlement as the night reaches its end.
Followed [by fear] as if by <s>Jaṭilā</s>, full of apprehension,
troubled by the weight of her heavy hips and breasts,
she went to <s>Vraja</s> with a gait both quick and slow and graceful,
the mistress [<s>Rādhā</s>], holding her garment and tresses in her hands.

children.text: na vyālād api sambibheti purataḥ sthāṇor yathā dūrato
children.translated_text: She does not fear even a serpent ahead as she does a [mere] post from afar;
she is not alarmed even by the roar of an elephant as by the cawing of crows;

children.text: naiveyaṃ timire'pi muhyati-tarāṃ kāmaṃ prakāśe yathā
children.translated_text: she is not at all confused even in darkness as she is in broad light —

children.text: tan manye virahe'pi naiva vidhurā kāntasya yoge yathā
children.translated_text: therefore I think she is not distressed even in separation as she is in union with her beloved.
With eyes wavering and darkened by the surge of fear and passion,
her heart's desire concealed by the eclipsing [darkness],
<s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s>, wishing to lead her to her own

children.text: gṛhaṃ ninīṣuḥ pathi tāṃ tad anvayāt
children.translated_text: home, followed her on the path.
With arrows of darting, restless glances cast here and there,
like messengers of the heart's agitated movements disturbed by fear,
<s>Rati Mañjarī</s> too, going before her,
warding off other people, followed her then.
Surrounded by them, unseen by the people of <s>Vraja</s>,
entering her home, she then settled upon her own bed.
Distressed by separation from her beloved, she then to her friend
openly expressed the pain of her heart, with faltering, tearful words:
'O <s>Lalitā</s>! Having just now taken me out of the house,
you bring me back in again just now —
the temptation of immersion in the nectar-ocean of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> embrace
was made in vain by you today!'
'That fierce-rayed one [the sun] who was just now seen
at the setting mountain, O friend! Does he now
desire to ascend the eastern mountain? Has tonight's
night become a flower of the sky [i.e., an impossibility]?'

children.text: dhiṅ me śrutiṃ dhig rasanāṃ dṛśaṃ ca dhik
children.translated_text: 'Shame on my ears! Shame on my tongue! And shame on my eyes!
Always afflicted with the fever of the burden of longing,

children.text: prāpur na pātuṃ lavam apy amuṣya yāḥ
children.translated_text: they could not drink even a drop of his
nectar of melodious voice, sweet flavor, and beautiful form.'
'Previously, even the path of indifference was reached;
union then, O innocent one, [brought] separation to you now.
The first showed the nectar of the imperishable one as its purpose;
the other makes one experience, alas, the bitter poison of <s>kālakūṭa</s>.'
Thus, even the words of her friend, this one
[<s>Rādhā</s>], supremely devoted through love, could not comprehend.
Then, to behold in dream her heart's lord once more,
she fell asleep on her bed — the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>.

children.text: anabhisārikāṃ kāñcit pṛcchantīṃ prati kācid āha-
children.translated_text: To a certain woman who was not a <s>abhisārikā</s> (one who goes to meet her lover) asking [about Rādhā], another said:

children.text: srastaṃ srastam udañcayaty adhiśiraḥ śyāmaṃ nicolāñcalaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Repeatedly lifting up over her head the dark edge of her shawl as it slips and slips,
bearing her body with its ornaments disheveled, with a loosened, weakened hand,

children.text: muktārdhām avarudhya veṇim alasa-syande kṣipantī dṛśau
children.translated_text: half-releasing her braid, casting languid, flowing glances,

children.text: kuñjāt paśya gṛhaṃ praviśya nibhṛtaṃ śete sakhī rādhikā
children.translated_text: see — entering her home from the bower, your friend <s>Rādhikā</s> lies down quietly.'
Having completed the abundance of amorous play, at the proper time, in their own abodes,
when <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable One) slept, as the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas) [merge] back into the Lord,
the friends, skilled in the arts of divine play, endowed with qualities,
went unnoticed to their own homes.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the first collection, named 'The Collection of the Pre-Dawn Pastimes,' in the <s>Śrī Bhāvanā-sāra-saṅgraha</s>.

children.text: paśyantīṃ svasutaṃ śaci bhagavatī saṅkīrtane vikṣataṃ
children.translated_text: Seeing her son wounded in <s>saṅkīrtana</s> (congregational chanting),

children.text: prātar hā katham eva te vapur idaṃ sūno babhūva kṣatam
children.translated_text: 'O son! How in the morning did your body become thus injured?' —

children.text: itthaṃ lālanataḥ svaputra-vanuṣi vyagrā spṛśantī muhus
children.translated_text: thus, anxious in her caressing, absorbed in attending to her son's body, touching him repeatedly,

children.text: talpāj jāgarayāñ cakāra yam ahaṃ taṃ gauracandraṃ bhaje
children.translated_text: she awakened him from bed — I worship that <s>Gauracandra</s> (the golden moon).

children.text: bhaktaiḥ sārddham upāgatair bhuvi nataiḥ śrīvāsa-guptādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: With devotees who came together and bowed on the ground — <s>Śrīvāsa</s>, <s>Gupta</s>, and others —

children.text: pṛcchadbhiḥ kuśalaṃ prage parimilan prakṣālya vaktraṃ jalaiḥ
children.translated_text: who inquired about his well-being in the morning; washing his face with water
scented with flowers and the like; pleasantly narrating the tale experienced in dream;

children.text: snātvādyād dhari-śeṣam odana-varaṃ yas taṃ ḥhi gauraṃ bhaje
children.translated_text: bathing and then eating the excellent rice remaining from <s>Hari's</s> [offering] — I worship that <s>Gaura</s>.
<s>Rādhā</s>, bathed and adorned, summoned by her friends in the morning to [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>] house in <s>Vraja</s>,
preparing food in that house, eating the remnants of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> meal;
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, awakened, having returned to the cow-shed, having completed the milking of cows,

children.text: susnātaṃ kṛta-bhojanaṃ sahacarais tāṃ cātha taṃ cāśraye
children.translated_text: well-bathed, having eaten with his companions — I take refuge in both her and him.
The maidservants adorned her bathed and anointed body with their own radiance,
with garlands of offered flowers, garments, and ornaments;
those who were devoted to fulfilling the desires of the two [<s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>],
equal in qualities and name to <s>Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī</s>.
They, whose single toe-line defeats the brilliance of lightning,
though they are indeed the very embodiments of cleverness, nevertheless,
not delighting even in the status of being a <s>yūtheśvarī</s> (group leader),
they eternally bathed in the nectar-ocean of servitude to her.
At the upper side within the mother-in-law's [<s>Jaṭilā's</s>] inner quarters,
a resplendent dwelling, the sole abode of excellent artistry,
by her father <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> himself, out of affection,

children.text: nirmāpitaṃ tad upamāpi tad eva nānyat
children.translated_text: was built — its comparison is itself alone, nothing else.
Pillars, porticos, crystal courtyards, arched gateways,
rafters, various chambers, windows, and platforms
shine there, illuminated by rows of jeweled lamps,
creating wonderful visions for the beholders' eyes.
Where the floor of sapphire and the eaves are dark as clouds,

children.text: haṃsālir apy upari rājati rājatī sā
children.translated_text: above shines that silvery row of swans,
which, seeing them as bearing the appearance of friends and foes,
the peacocks spread and then contract their rows of tail-feathers.
The platforms for sitting, sleeping, eating, adorning, and so forth —

children.text: vedīr vimṛjya parilipya viśodhya tās tāḥ
children.translated_text: wiping, anointing, and thoroughly cleaning each one,
spreading woolen blankets above, with pearls properly placed,
they tied the festive canopies high with great delight.
One polished vessels of jewels and gold;
another brought milk suitable for the occasion;
on a jeweled four-legged platform covered with colorful cloth,
another placed a pillow to recline upon.
The garments, jeweled and gem-studded ornaments

children.text: mṛṣṭāni yatra nihitāny atha sampu aṃ tat
children.translated_text: that had been cleaned and stored the previous day — that casket,
opening it with loudly jingling rows of bangles,
one ground sandalwood paste, camphor, and <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron).
Another arranged flowers with flowers themselves,
with colorful tiaras, bracelets, armlets, necklaces, and girdles;
tinted with jasmine, clove, catechu, and other [fragrances],
one tied delightful betel-leaf vine rolls.
Meanwhile, in every direction, with the sounds arising from churning yogurt,
with the unrestrained chanting of the <s>Vedas</s> by the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
with the lowing of herds of cows and calves that drown out
each other's calls — there were obstacles between them.
With waves of nectar of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa's</s> fame and glory
being spread by crowds of excellent panegyrists,
with the calls of <s>śārī</s> (mynas), parrots, <s>kalaviṅkas</s> (sparrows), peacocks,
and <s>kokilas</s> (cuckoos) — sounds gradually increasing,
as the multitudes of people awakened and the day [began],
occupied with contemplation of duties to be done, still lying in bed —
among the groups of married women thirsting for a moment's sight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
whose minds were fixed upon the house of <s>Nanda</s>,
[<s>Yaśodā</s>], whose life was [sustained by] seeing the lotus-face of her granddaughter's [husband],
the one named <s>Mukharā</s> (the Talkative One), who suddenly approached,
who was a casket filled with the jewels of maternal affection —
calling out, 'O <s>Rādhā</s>! Where are you, daughter?'
Though crooked by nature,
desiring the prosperity of her own
son, <s>Jaṭilā</s>, troubled, went
near [<s>Mukharā</s>] and then said to her:
'For the progeny and increase of wealth of my son,
this daughter-in-law, O wise one, must be directed
to the auspicious bathing, adorning, and other [rites],
for the worship of the sun, for the sake of ten million cows.'
'Disregard of the commands of the queen of one's own cowherd settlement,
and disregard of instructions on duties by the unknowing —
thus daily instructs the wise in purpose,
<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, who has been informed by me.'
'Therefore, O noble lady, your granddaughter,
adorned with all auspicious marks,
arrange [her] so that all prosperity
may come to my son.'
Then she addressed the bride: 'Daughter!
Rise quickly from the bed and perform the house-worship;
having completed the rite of auspicious bathing,
make the offering of worship to the sun.'
'The dawn has arrived, yet even so
the granddaughter sleeps!' — saying this repeatedly,
<s>Mukharā</s>, her body melting with affection, entering
the bedroom, said this to her:
'Arise, dear child, from your bed, O deeply sleeping one!
Have you forgotten today's turn for the sun's [worship]?
Having bathed, perform the morning offering to him,
and quickly prepare the worship-offering for him.'
Awakened by her words, then
<s>Viśākhā</s>, rising languidly,
'O friend! Quickly arise,
arise!' — she said hastily.
By their words, the innocent one on the bed
repeatedly awakening and falling asleep again,
like a royal <s>haṃsī</s> (swan) in a lake disturbed
by waves — her body languid from love-weariness.
Then, knowing the right moment,
<s>Rati Mañjarī</s> grasped
the auspicious lotus-feet
of the friend of the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.
Thus, awakened by many,
she rose from her magnificent bed.
Then, seeing her wearing a yellow garment,
<s>Mukharā</s>, her heart suspicious, said this:
'This garment on your friend's chest, O friend, the color of molten gold,

children.text: vasanam urasi dṛṣṭaṃ yat sakhī te bibharti
children.translated_text: was seen in the evening as belonging to <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) —

children.text: kim idam ayi viśākhe! hā pramādaḥ pramādo
children.translated_text: what is this, O <s>Viśākhā</s>! Alas, a blunder, a blunder!
See the conduct of this one, from such a pure lineage!'
Hearing those words, her mind startled, seeing in her heart the friend's
yellow garment with a flickering glance,

children.text: hā kim etad iti tāṃ ca diśantī
children.translated_text: 'Ah, what is this!' — indicating to her,
<s>Viśākhā</s> quickly spoke to the old woman:
'O blind one by nature! Through the gaps in the lattice, by the touch of the rays
of the sun risen at dawn, with the splendor of her golden body's radiance overflowing,

children.text: vayasyāyāḥ śyāmaṃ vasanam api pīti-kṛtam idaṃ
children.translated_text: even this dark garment of my friend has been made to appear yellow —

children.text: kuto mugdhe śaṅkāṃ jarati kuruṣe śuddha-matiṣu
children.translated_text: why, O foolish old woman, do you harbor suspicion toward those of pure mind?'
<s>Lalitā</s> and the other chief
friends, each from their own homes,
came hastily to their friend's
side, with stumbling gaits.
By their words, with accumulated deceptions,
having sent away
<s>Mukharā</s>, while the others
desired to see her there —
when all the friends had gathered one by one,
engaged in mutual laughter and jest among themselves,
seated together in a circle,
upon the jeweled and golden four-legged platforms,
the meeting with <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> itself being the sole shower of rain
for the crop of all happiness — knowing this in her heart,
<s>Śyāmalā</s>, knowing the right time,
embraced by her [<s>Rādhā</s>], with great beauty, was there then.
'O <s>Śyāmā</s>! You were just now being thought of by me,
and by fate you have been brought to the path of my eyes;

children.text: tadvat sa tarṣa-vi apī phalayiṣyate ced
children.translated_text: if that tree of longing shall bear fruit,
then indeed I shall count even today as a good morning.'
'Alas! This [tree], constantly and greatly growing,
forever being watered by friends, O beautiful one!

children.text: nādyāpi yat phalam adhād ayi! ko 'tra hetur
children.translated_text: Has not yet borne fruit — what is the reason here?
Ah, when shall I behold [its fruit] with sudden eagerness?'

children.text: rādhe! sa te na phalito yadi tat phaliṣyaty
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rādhā</s>! If it has not borne fruit for you, it will;

children.text: āścaryam asya phalam apy alasāṅgi! buddhye
children.translated_text: I perceive that its fruit too will be wonderful, O languid-limbed one!
Even while being savored, its fragrance, with its captivated bees,
loudly proclaims itself as if never before experienced.'
'If the eyelash-row is reddened by its [the fruit's] juice —

children.text: nārañji kañja-mukhi! tan na tad apy apaśyaḥ
children.translated_text: orange-hued, O lotus-faced one! — did you not see even that?
From the intensity of tasting which, the lip becomes wounded —'

children.text: āgāt tathāpi tad aho! na kadāpy abhuṅkthāḥ
children.translated_text: came nevertheless, yet alas! you never partook [of it].
O <s>Śyāmā</s>! You too, enough — with a deeply hidden wound in your heart unnoticed by me,

children.text: svānta-vraṇā hasasi māṃ yad ato bravīmi
children.translated_text: you laugh at me; therefore I say:

children.text: vidyud vihanti timiraṃ niśi yad dṛśos tat
children.translated_text: Lightning dispels darkness at night, but that [darkness] of the eyes

children.text: sadyaḥ punar dviguṇayed iti bhoḥ pratīhi
children.translated_text: it immediately doubles again — believe this, O friend!
O <s>Rādhā</s>! This treasure-house of arts (<s>kalānidhi</s>, the moon) has been brought by <s>Vidhi</s> (Providence);
he anointed you with his fingertips, ever flowing with nectar.

children.text: yat tat-kalāḥ svayam aho kucayor bibharṣi
children.translated_text: That you yourself bear his digits (<s>kalās</s>) upon your breasts — alas!
and yet you invite the reproach of resembling lightning.

children.text: śyāme! sa me sakhi! dadau na kalaṅkam eva
children.translated_text: O <s>Śyāmā</s>! He, my friend, gave me not merely a blemish (<s>kalaṅka</s>);

children.text: satyaṃ kalānidhir asāv iti vaḥ pratītaḥ
children.translated_text: truly, he is recognized by you all as that treasure of arts (<s>kalānidhi</s>, the moon).
To which my <s>cakora</s>-like eyes sometimes

children.text: jyotsnā-kaṇaṃ yad api tan na punar nikāmam
children.translated_text: receive even a droplet of moonlight, yet never to their full satisfaction.
O <s>Rādhā</s>! Tell me clearly — the celestial river of nectar flowing at night, arising from your lotus-face,
sweeping away

children.text: tāpaṃ nimajjayatu māṃ svam anu prabhāte
children.translated_text: the anguish, let it immerse me; and at dawn thereafter
how could any other duty of mine be well-accomplished without that?
O <s>Śyāmā</s>! When in the bower-dwelling, a stream of fresh dark-blue radiance

children.text: dhārā yadā snapayituṃ niśi māṃ pravṛttā
children.translated_text: commenced to bathe me at night,
at that very moment, to the arena of the play of the five-arrowed one (<s>Pañcaśara</s>, Kāmadeva),

children.text: bhūmiṃ ca kena ca kāñcana yāpitā'sam
children.translated_text: I was transported by someone to some golden [place].
Speaking thus, she fell into a swoon that generates the supreme, ultimate bliss;
she immediately entered the state of loss of consciousness.

children.text: kadāyātā śyāme punar iti hi pṛṣṭāham adhunā-
children.translated_text: "When did you come, O <s>Śyāmā</s>?" — thus I was asked again; "Just now
I have come," saying this, she inquired of her who had just regained awareness.
Your languidly swaying body reveals its own weariness;
your two arms are like a wilted lotus-stalk shoot.
This cloth covering your teeth is insipid; [upon] the surface of [your] cheeks
the delicate decorative leaf-patterns are disturbed — what is this state of yours?
Like a fresh creeper battered by the wind,
like a new lotus-plant crushed by an elephant,
like a most tender, fresh jasmine-garland shaken
by an intoxicated bee — so do you appear today.
Even one long desired thus,
O beloved, some exceedingly rare one has indeed been obtained.
Then how is it that from our lot, differently,
the wish-fulfilling vine of fortune has borne fruit, O friend?
Thus, being asked with affectionate words and respectful care,
her moon-like face veiled by her garment, her heart transparent — alas, she,
generating delight among the friends gathered at her side,
with her gaze cast upon the ground, smilingly replied:

children.text: kvāhaṃ sthitā kva calitā kva ca vā sa panthā
children.translated_text: "Where was I standing? Where did I go? And where was that path?
By whom was I led to his side, O lotus-eyed one?
Or what happened to me when I arrived there?

children.text: jānāmy ahaṃ yadi tadā bhavatī na vetti
children.translated_text: If I know, then you do not know either."

children.text: vyāpāro manasaś ca yatra na gataḥ sambhāvanābhāvato
children.translated_text: "Where the activity of the mind has not reached, due to the impossibility of even conceiving it —

children.text: yat svapnaḥ kim athendra-jālam athavā bhrāntiḥ sudīrghaiva me
children.translated_text: was it a dream, or was it magic (<s>indrajāla</s>), or indeed a very long delusion of mine?

children.text: tat kiṃ hlādi kim ārtidaṃ kim ubhayaṃ kiṃvā na tan nāpi tac-
children.translated_text: Was that joyful, or pain-giving, or both, or neither this nor that —
it caused the melting of the heart and produced a swoon of the mind."
Then <s>Śyāmā</s> said:
"The skill in studying the arts of amorous play

children.text: na syād ataḥ kim api no bhavatī viveda
children.translated_text: cannot be [acquired] all at once; therefore you have not understood something."
"Again, O friend, from the teacher of love-sports,
study diligently, if you wish to become the most learned."
Then Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s> said:
"O mother! O beautiful-faced one! I go to his side;
from afar, he is one from whom the eyes should be turned away.

children.text: adhyetu nāma bhavatī tata eva tat te
children.translated_text: Let your ladyship study from that [teacher] indeed — may that

children.text: pāṇḍityam eva manaso rasadaṃ mama syāt
children.translated_text: erudition of yours be the source of delight for my heart."
"O fair-toothed one! Pearls [are scattered] by whose scratching nails,
flung amid the bowers, these, surrounded by garlands of lotuses, their luster [glowing] in bower after bower —
how was it that this glorious <s>Hari</s>, while you, O doe-eyed one, laid the ocean of beauty upon the terrace of your breasts,

children.text: sa śrīmān hariṇekṣaṇe! harir abhūn netreṇa baddhas tvayā?
children.translated_text: was bound by you with [just] a glance?"

children.text: ko 'yaṃ kṛṣṇa iti vyudasyati dhṛtiṃ yas tanvi karṇaṃ viśan
children.translated_text: "Who is this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who, entering the ear, O slender one, destroys composure?

children.text: rāgāndhe! kim idaṃ sadaiva bhavatī tasyor asi krīḍati
children.translated_text: O one blinded by passion! What is this — you are always his plaything?

children.text: hāsyaṃ mā kuru mohite! tvam adhunā nyastāsya haste mayā
children.translated_text: Do not jest, O deluded one! You have now been placed in his hands by me.

children.text: satyaṃ satyam asau dṛgaṅganam agād adyaiva vidyun-nibhaḥ
children.translated_text: Truly, truly, he, radiant as lightning, has today entered the pathway of [your] eyes."
Overwhelmed by the weight of bashfulness, remaining utterly silent,
her companion [sat]; to hear the account of the beloved's amorous play,
taking hold of her chin, she then

children.text: hy aty āgrahīd ālīm atha pravaktum
children.translated_text: earnestly pressed her friend to speak.

children.text: priya-sakhi! mama vṛttaṃ pṛccha mā bhāgyam īdṛk
children.translated_text: "Dear friend! Ask about my experience — do not [ask about] such fortune!

children.text: kva nu mama kathayeyaṃ tvayy ahaṃ tān vilāsān
children.translated_text: Where indeed could I describe to you those love-sports?

children.text: dhṛtavati karam eva śyāmale kvāsa kāhaṃ
children.translated_text: When [he] merely held my hand — O dark one, where was I, who was I?

children.text: kim iva ca karako 'sau kiṃ vyadhān na smarāmi
children.translated_text: What indeed was that hand of his? What did he do? I do not remember."
"He braids [your] hair with clusters of divine flowers; at the parting-line — alas!

children.text: sindūraṃ nidadhāti kajjala-mayīṃ nirmāti rekhāṃ dṛśoḥ
children.translated_text: He applies <s>sindūra</s> (vermilion); he draws a line of <s>kajjala</s> (collyrium) upon [your] eyes;

children.text: divyaṃ vāsayate dukūlam asakṛt tāmbūlam apy āśayed
children.translated_text: he dresses [you] in divine silk garments repeatedly, and offers <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) too —

children.text: itthambhūta-ratiḥ sakhā tava na māṃ talpe nidhatte'ṅkataḥ
children.translated_text: such is your lover's devotion, friend — yet does he not place me upon the bed from [his] lap?"
"Always he holds his moon-face before my face with unblinking gaze;
always he gazes only at my face, ever absorbed in conversation with me alone;

children.text: ādhāyaiva śayīta māṃ hṛdi mayaivāvartayet pārśvakaṃ
children.translated_text: placing me upon his heart, he would sleep; turning his side only with me —

children.text: sakhyus te sakhi! sarva-nāgara-maṇeḥ prītiḥ kathaṃ varṇyatām?
children.translated_text: O friend! How can the love of your companion, that jewel among all gallants, be described?"
"The amorous gestures of the slayer of <s>Keśī</s>, O friend,
burn my heart like <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison);
his virtues pierce my vital points like wood-boring worms;
love is transformative — a wound in the heart, like a heart-wound indeed."

children.text: no vidmaḥ kim u gauravaṃ gurukule kaulīnya-rakṣā-vidhau
children.translated_text: "We know not whether [there remains] respect for the teacher's house, or care for preserving family honor;

children.text: na śraddhā kim u durjanokti-garala-jvālāsu kiṃ no bhayam
children.translated_text: whether [there is] faith, or whether [we have] no fear of the flames of poison-like words of the wicked —

children.text: udvegādan avasthitaṃ mama manaḥ kasyāpi megha-tviṣo
children.translated_text: my mind, beset by agitation, has been established [in fixation] upon a certain youth of cloud-like complexion,

children.text: yūnaḥ śrotra-gatair ghuṇair iva guṇair antaḥ kṛtaṃ jarjaram
children.translated_text: and has been rendered hollow within by his virtues, entering through the ears, like wood-boring worms."
"O <s>Rādhā</s>! When the very fragrance of whose lotus-face thus
blinds the family of noble women from afar, O friend,
that you, drinking his exceedingly sweet, delicious nectar,

children.text: citta-bhramas tava madād iti naiva citram
children.translated_text: experience bewilderment of mind from intoxication — that is no wonder at all."
At this point, <s>Madhurikā</s> arrived and, being asked by them,
spoke sweetly: "Listen to this, O friends!
For some [purpose], having arrived today at the house of the king of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: prāptādya kautukam aho yad uṣasy apaśyam
children.translated_text: what a wonder I beheld at dawn!"
"<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, the venerable one, bestower of all accomplishments,
wearing saffron garments, fair-complexioned, with white hair, slightly tall,
desirous of seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, arose from her bed at the sounds of the birds."
Then, at dawn, having completed her daily rites,
with her mind exceedingly agitated with love for <s>Acyuta</s>,
filled with the moon of divine love, <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>
swiftly reached the abode of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>.
Wearing a fine linen garment bound with a cord upon her broad hips,
her pair of breasts dripping with maternal affection, trembling, the beautiful-browed one —
her bangles and earrings swaying as her arms moved from the exertion of pulling the rope,
her face perspiring, jasmine flowers slipping from her braid — she was churning [yogurt].
At the turn of night, the majestic sound
arising from the churning of yogurt by the cowherd women,
pervading the sphere of the celestial city at once,
reminds the hosts of gods of the festival of the churning of the ocean.
Its courtyard beautiful, strewn with scattered drops of milk-products raised by the churning rod,
filled with people tender with love, its interior adorned with many kinds of jewels,
overflowing with waves of milk, with <s>Acyuta</s> sleeping blissfully on his splendid bed —
seeing the abode of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> as if it were <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island), she was filled with delight.
Seeing her arrival,
as if the very splendor of austerity [had come] in person,
the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, supremely discerning,
knowledgeable of propriety, rose with joy.
"Come, O venerable one!" — thus [addressing] the one honored by all of <s>Vraja</s>,
"Welcome! I bow to your ladyship" —
having spoken thus to the one bowing nearby,
she embraced the mother of <s>Mukunda</s>.
Having congratulated her with blessings,
eager to see <s>Govinda</s>,
she inquired about the welfare
of her [family] — husband, sons, and cattle.
Having conveyed her welfare to her as well,
together with her who was filled with longing,
the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, eager,
entered the bedchamber of her son.
With her twisted hair-locks fastened by a cord, her parting adorned with a shining drop of <s>sindūra</s> (vermilion),
wearing the decoration of the stage of beauty but not excessively,
her pair of eyes tearful, released [in emotion] upon <s>Govinda's</s> face, dark as a fresh blue lotus,
dark-complexioned with wondrous raiment — may the queen of <s>Goṣṭha</s> (the cowherd settlement) protect you!

children.text: paryaṅke nyasya savyaṃ tad-upari nihita-svāṅgabhārātha pāṇiṃ
children.translated_text: Placing her left hand on the couch, resting her body's weight upon it,
touching <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> body with her other lotus-hand, slightly bent at the waist,

children.text: siñcanty ānanda-bāṣpaiḥ snuta-kuca-payasāṃ dhārayā cāsya talpaṃ
children.translated_text: sprinkling his bed with tears of joy and with streams of milk flowing from her breasts,

children.text: vatsottiṣṭhāśu nidrāṃ tyaja mukha-kamalaṃ darśayety āha mātā
children.translated_text: "O darling, rise quickly! Abandon sleep! Show [me] your lotus-face!" — thus spoke the mother.
<s>Madhurikā</s> said:

children.text: gāndharvike! śṛṇu yad anyad abhūd vicitraṃ
children.translated_text: "O <s>Gāndharvikā</s>! Listen to what else wondrous happened —
seeing a dark-blue garment on his body, being examined,

children.text: tām āha saiva bhagavaty ayi goṣṭha-rājñi!
children.translated_text: that very venerable lady said to the queen of <s>Goṣṭha</s>:
His garment has been exchanged with <s>Rāma's</s> (Balarāma's) cloth."
"It is merely the reflection of the ruby upon [your] lap
that shines as a reddish glow upon your cheek, O <s>Mādhava</s>!"

children.text: ity ukta eva sa tayā nija-pāṇinā taṃ
children.translated_text: Thus told by her, he with his own hand immediately
rubbed away that portion [which was really] the color of your lip-rouge.
"Arise, dear child! The night has come to an end;
behold the sun, beautiful as it rises on the horizon."
"Radiant with graceful beauty in the observance of the dawn-rites,
your young attendants are entering your bedchamber."
"Chanting Victory! Victory! with well-composed voice,
this [bird], devoted, has commenced to awaken you with affection, O dear child —
this parrot of yours, nourished by your own palm,
speaking beautifully sweet words, delighted in his golden cage."
"This lethargy of yours, rooted in the burden of sleep-laziness —
abandon slumber and become inclined to wakefulness!"

children.text: itthaṃ kareṇa mṛdunā muhur aṅgam aṅgam
children.translated_text: Thus, gently touching limb after limb with her hand,
she embraced him with both arms.
Hearing and experiencing his mother's artful speech and most affectionate embrace,

children.text: śrutvānubhūya ca tadaiva sa samyag ūham
children.translated_text: he then fully deliberated.
With a yawn preceded by stretching of the limbs,
he entered the state of wakefulness with curiosity.
In the time-appropriate and skillfully performed services,
filled with intense, surpassing love, free from agitation,
having expertly instructed the young male and female attendants in [her] presence,
the wife of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> departed to her own home.
Meanwhile, <s>Gobhaṭa</s>, <s>Bhadrasena</s>, <s>Subala</s>, Śrī <s>Stokakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>,
Śrī <s>Dāma</s>, <s>Ujjvala</s>, <s>Dāma</s>, <s>Kiṅkiṇi</s>, <s>Sudāma</s>, and other friends, from [their] homes
came swiftly, joyfully met Śrī <s>Sīriṇa</s> (Balarāma) in the courtyard,

children.text: kṛṣṇottiṣṭha nijeṣṭa-goṣṭham aya bho ity āhvayantaḥ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: and stood calling out: "O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! Rise! Come to your beloved cowherd-station, O friend!"

children.text: hī hī prabhātaṃ kim u bho vayasyā
children.translated_text: "Alas, alas! It is dawn — what, O friends?
Our companion still sleeps even now?
Then I shall wake him!" — declaring thus,
<s>Madhumaṅgala</s> too arose from his own bed.
Saying "Arise, O friend!"
chattering, [heading toward] the bedchamber of <s>Hari</s>,
stumbling in his gait, drowsy with sleep,
<s>Madhumaṅgala</s> entered.
Awakened from sleep by his voice,
the Lord wished to rise,
yet was unable to rise,
his eyes filled with dizziness for a moment.
"Arise! Let me perform your face-washing.
Why is <s>Bala's</s> (Balarāma's) garment here on your body?"
Saying thus, she removed the dark
garment from his body and spoke to <s>Āryā</s> (Yaśodā):

children.text: ayi bhagavati! paśyāco itaṃ me'sya sūnoḥ
children.translated_text: "O venerable one! See the condition of this son of mine —
his body, tender as a lotus, by those [boys] eager in wrestling sports,
with their sharp claw-like nails, has been made exceedingly variegated with colored streaks —
alas! What shall I do about these restless groups of children?"
Hearing even the artfully worded speech
of his own mother, laden with affection,
the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Murāri</s>, Kṛṣṇa)
became one whose eyes darted with embarrassment.
Suspecting <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to be apprehensive,
the witty <s>baṭu</s> (young brahmin, Madhumaṅgala),
skilled in jest, [addressed] the mother
whose heart was melting with affection — <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> spoke:
"Truly, O mother! [His] lady friend,
though restrained by me throughout the night,
sported with this greedy one,
restless in amorous play, in the bowers."
Then, his childhood playfulness made manifest,
