striving to open his eyes again and again,

children.text: paśyan puraḥ svāṃ jananīṃ hariḥ punar
children.translated_text: Seeing his own mother before him, <s>Hari</s> again
closed his eyes, he whose face-lotus bore a smile.
Hearing the words of the wife of the king of <s>Vraja</s>,
and observing <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> childish behavior
which concealed the inner sentiments of his mother,
<s>Paurṇamāsī</s> spoke to him with a preceding smile:
'With throngs of girlfriends and endless series of great sports,

children.text: pariśrāntas tvaṃ yat svapiṣi sumate yogyam iha tat
children.translated_text: you are exhausted, O wise one, and so you sleep — that is fitting here.

children.text: anālokya tvāṃ bhos tṛṣitam api no tarṇaka-kulaṃ
children.translated_text: But look! Without seeing you, the thirsty herd of calves

children.text: dhayaty ūdhaḥ kintu vraja-kula-pate jāgṛhi tataḥ
children.translated_text: suckles the udders nonetheless. O lord of the cowherd clan, therefore awaken!'
'Arise, O son of the lord of the cowherds! Nearby
see — your elder brother, together with your companions,
about to set out for the cow-station, yet waiting
for you, stands in the courtyard with the calves.'
Raising both fists upward,
he stretched his languid, slow-moving limbs.
With a web of tooth-rays spreading through his yawn,
dark as a <s>tamāla</s> tree, he rose from the bed.
In the abundance of opening and closing [of his eyes],
as if the states of waking and sleeping were intermingled,
held as if by drowsiness distressed at [its] separation [from him] —
the pair of eyes of him who had arisen shone forth.
Then, seated on a portion of the bed,
his pair of lotus-feet placed upon the earth,
'I bow to you, O blessed one!' — thus
he spoke, his voice faltering from the arising of a yawn.
Then, with the touching of her palms from foot to head —
reciting the mantra 'avyādajaḥ' ('may the Unborn protect') at each limb —
having quickly blessed all his limbs, then with upward gaze,
the queen entreated with a somewhat plaintive tone.
'O Lord of lords! By you alone, after a long time, this son
was given, having become the very life of his own kinfolk.
He is to be protected, O Lord, by you alone with the weight of your compassion.

children.text: svenaiva kām apacitiṃ tava vedmi kartum
children.translated_text: By my own [efforts], what tribute can I know to offer you?'
With the <s>āratrika</s> (waving of lights) in a vessel of jeweled auspicious lamps,
resplendent, conquering the beauty of assemblies,
placing [the lamp] in the lotus-like palms, joyfully,
the maidservants performed the <s>nīrājana</s> (lamp-waving ceremony) for the prince.
With most charming turbans bound upon their heads,
their beautiful limbs fragrant with the sweet scent of lotus filaments,

children.text: śyāmāḥ sitāś ca haritā aruṇāś ca pītā
children.translated_text: dark, fair, green, ruddy, and yellow —
whatever [complexions] they had, all were endowed with magnificent qualities.
By those very [servants] whose nature was solely the experience of bliss,
whose forms were innately divine each day, like young princes,
by the groups of maidservants and also by the noble groups of manservants,
various services were rendered, their necklaces swinging.
Ascending the couch to the jeweled seat of four [legs],
whose form gleamed with the splendor of the blessed footstool,
they received him, beautifully seated, with overjoyed hearts,
and then, gathering together, performed beautiful attendance.
Placing upon his palm the stream offered by them,
of exceedingly lovely water fragrant with camphor,
filling his mouth for a delightful rinse,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> gently washed the chamber of his lotus-face.
Wiping with a piece of beautiful, soft, fine, white cloth
his hands and face, he who had an artless smile,
accepted from their hands the soft tooth-cleaning stick
placed upon his palm — the most tender and the lightest.
With that soft twig of the <s>kalpa-druma</s> (wish-fulfilling tree),
adorned with the great brilliance of jeweled rings,
he gently scrubbed his row of teeth — a delight to the watching eyes —
his pair of earrings swaying to and fro.
With a tongue-scraper of jewels and gold,
held by the span between thumb and forefinger,
O king, he scraped the jewel-crested tongue — charming,
surpassing the redness of <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), a connoisseur of flavors.
Again he washed his face with pure water,

children.text: bhūyo mamārja ca kadāpi na codviveja
children.translated_text: and again wiped it, never feeling any discomfort.
A blessed mirror, offered by a maidservant with darting eyes —
<s>Lakṣmī</s> herself — he made it witness to the purity of his mouth-washing.
With a ruby comb that had come into the chamber of his lotus-hand,
producing the beautiful sound of bangles and comb,
a certain maidservant then performed the combing of his hair,
her face bearing an artless smile.
Someone removed his nightclothes and,
skilled in the arts, properly dressed him in an inner garment.
Then she bound the turban upon his head, and at the beginning of the day,
having washed his feet with water and wiped them.
The cowherds, though eager-minded to milk the cows, made futile efforts,
and so did the groups of calves —

children.text: cūṣanta eva na payaḥ kaṇa-mātram āsām
children.translated_text: they could not suck even a drop of milk
from the udders today, hence they were distressed.
'Your cows on the path, their eyes filled with held-back tears,

children.text: na prasravanty apagatān na lihanti vatsān
children.translated_text: neither let their milk flow nor lick the calves that have gone away.
Lowing, their sound filling the circle of directions, the delay —

children.text: soḍhuṃ darāpi na hi samprati śaknuvanti
children.translated_text: they are unable to endure even slightly now.'

children.text: ity eva kenacid upetya sa goduhokto
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by a certain cowherd who had approached, he, the milker of cows,
bathing his mother's face with the nectar of his gentle smile,
delighting her with [smiles] that proclaimed his own bliss, his lotus-face
reddened with <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) — admiring it well, he arose.
'O <s>Balabhadra</s>! Having finished the milking, together with your younger brother,

children.text: mallājiraṃ vrajasi cet kuru mā vilambam
children.translated_text: if you go to the wrestling arena, do not delay.
I shall perform your <s>nirmañcana</s> (protective rite) in just a moment.

children.text: sārdhaṃ vihṛtya sakhibhir drutam ehi bhoktum
children.translated_text: After sporting with your friends, come quickly to eat.'

children.text: śrutveti mātṛ-giram āha harir na mātaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing his mother's words, <s>Hari</s> said, 'O Mother!

children.text: pratyeṣi māṃ yad amum eva vadasy athaivam
children.translated_text: You send me back, yet you say this very [thing to him] — thus indeed,

children.text: śiṣṭo 'graṇīḥ punar amīṣv aham eka eva
children.translated_text: he is the obedient leader among these [brothers], while I alone am the [mischievous] one.

children.text: no ced amuṣya vaśatāṃ kim uri kariṣye?
children.translated_text: Otherwise, what shall I do under his authority?'

children.text: śiṣṭo yathā tvam asi vatsa! nijātibālyam
children.translated_text: 'How obedient you are, O child! Your [nature] since your earliest infancy

children.text: ārabhya tat khalu vidanty akhilāḥ purandhryaḥ
children.translated_text: is well known to all the noble ladies of <s>Vraja</s>,
who, through the pain of loss to their own homes,

children.text: phut-kartum āpur iha no katidheti soce
children.translated_text: have been unable to exclaim "Phut!" [in annoyance] — how many times! — thus I lament.'
With the splendor of lightning surpassing rows of lightning streaks, radiant,
a lotus clasped in the bud of his left hand,
holding a small golden milking pail,

children.text: mātrā tayā sakhi! rayād adhikaṃ vireje
children.translated_text: given by that mother — O friend! — he shone exceedingly.
With a slow, hanging gait that mocked the gait of a young elephant,
his anklet-bells jingling and tinkling,
the splendor of his swaying locks, jeweled earrings, and lustrous braid
bathing the moon-disc of his face in waves of radiance,
his yellow upper garment fluttering in playful, sportive dance,
the rays of his dark, glorious body leaping upward in splendor,
with his swinging garland as circumference, the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem rising
like a sun, his tinkling foot-ornaments kissing the garland,
emerging from the beautiful mansion, approaching forward,
giving joy to the eyes of his mother and her women,
receiving the parasol held by servants, its radiance unobstructed,
and the betel-offering — he reached the top of the gateway.
Resting upon the outer terrace there,

children.text: kā kutra kiṃ kuruta ity anusandadhānaḥ
children.translated_text: looking about — 'Who is where? What is she doing?' — thus investigating,
employing his eyes upon the water-pots, [he shone forth]

children.text: preṣṭhair miladbhir abhitaḥ sa rarāja mitraiḥ
children.translated_text: surrounded by his dearest friends who arrived from all sides for jesting.
On the lotus of his face — knower of the flavor of ear-tales composed by them —
a certain smile arose,
whose full meaning — am I capable of unfolding?
Let the bee of your heart, O friend, investigate it.
In the great sweetness of the curves of his turban,

children.text: tātkālike kila na kasya mano nyamāṅkṣīt
children.translated_text: at that moment, whose mind was not captivated?
And the splendors of the king-gems in the network of golden threads
crowned upon it — are they even describable?
With their fragrance spreading abundantly, accompanied by the sounds of anklets and such,
forcibly having climbed upon the balconies,
by the rows of women moving on the path to the cow-shed,

children.text: netrāmbujaiḥ sa katidhā nahi pūjyate sma
children.translated_text: he was worshipped in how many ways with their lotus-eyes!
That sweetness, seasoned with the flavor of his various charms,
of the most beloved one, being served [to them] —
though it cooled the fever of separation from him,

children.text: tene ca taṃ śata-guṇaṃ tṛṣam edhayantī
children.translated_text: it also increased their thirst a hundredfold.
The surge of joy spread stillness to the ears,
while the fever born of thirst entered the eyes.
Sudden, incomparable, neighboring wealth
always inflicts pain upon those who dwell alongside it.
Then she, supremely devoted in love, spoke —
'O beautiful-faced one! Only those women are the most fortunate
who constantly sport, O fair-eyed ones, in the ocean of his beauty's play,
their limbs washed in liquid gold.'

children.text: janmaiva hanta kim abhūn mama gokule'smiṃs
children.translated_text: 'Alas! Was my birth in this <s>Gokula</s>

children.text: tan mādhurīṃ na yad urī-kurute kadāpi
children.translated_text: such that it never makes that sweetness its own?
In that dark, exceedingly restless one, even a trace [of attachment]

children.text: no sambhaved iha bhave dhṛtir ity avehi
children.translated_text: in the heart — know that in this life, steadfastness cannot exist.'

children.text: śyāmāha yāmi! lalite! śṛṇu yāmi gehaṃ
children.translated_text: '<s>Śyāmā</s> said: "I go! O <s>Lalitā</s>! Listen — I go home.

children.text: sampraty amūṃ prati mamāstu girāṃ virāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Now let there be a cessation of my words regarding her.
You, O one bound by longing, take this <s>Padminī</s>
to this mansion of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, O <s>Kṛṣṇekṣaṇālinī</s>, and present her."'
Distraught from separation from her beloved, her composure lost, she at that time
reckoned even a moment to be an age or a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle).

children.text: yad akhilam api kṛtyaṃ kāritā kiṅkarībhiḥ
children.translated_text: Since all her duties were performed by her maidservants,
habit alone was the cause of this [mechanical] practice.
Then, that row of all her friends, bathed by their own attendants,
wearing appropriate garments and ornaments,
conquered even the beauty born of the ocean of autumn moonlight,
churned, as it were, by the radiance of her own lotus-feet.
One brought a seat made of the finest jewels;
another placed the blessed footstool beneath it.
One brought the vessels for face-washing;
another arranged the implements for tooth-cleaning.
Rising from the surface of the bed, seated on a golden seat,
her usual composure loosening as sleep ended,
she, with lotus-feet placed upon the footstool,
shone forth, honored by her good attendants.
With waters offered from the tip of the ewer's spout,
cupped in the hollow of her mouth,
more fragrant in their rush than its [natural] fragrance,
reddened by contact with the blessed lotus-palm,
deposited into the hands of her dear companion,
well-perfumed with the dust of abundant camphor,
pervaded by her friends skilled in all arts of play —
she thoroughly cleansed her lotus-face with those waters.
Water, repeatedly cupped from her palm,
was swirled up to the teeth and palate;
lovely with the rising of both moving cheeks,
bearing a [gurgling] sound — she quietly spat it out.
Scattering the spreading locks upon her head,
with the touches of the fingers of her left hand above,
then, the forehead, cheeks, and eyes having been made
equal in luster, gleaming — she washed [her face] thrice.
A tooth-brush, radiant with spread-out luster,
placed for the teeth, set down by her companion,
assuming the appearance of a closed lotus instantly —
the beautiful-eyed one took it with her tender hand.
Swinging with the motion of the tied bracelet, silent
bangles, with uplifted earrings — by her
she performed it, cleaning her teeth, [spreading] a luster
that leapt up in particles, beautiful, clinging [to them].
Then the beautiful-toothed one took up the bow-shaped,
jeweled tongue-scraper,
with two fingers of both her soft hands,
from the hand of her companion, with gentle satisfaction.
As she scraped her tongue, resembling a fresh petal,
then, with her head bowed and trembling,
her face covered with disheveled locks,
bearing a smile, she shone forth.
She cleaned both the outer and inner [mouth] thoroughly.
Then, of the moon[-like] face, with both hands washed,
with a lovely cloth offered by her attendants,
she gently removed the water-drops.
In the jeweled mirror held by her companion,
witness to [her own] admiration, seeing [her reflection],
she washed her face with the nectar of a smile,
marking the signs of moments with her beloved.
Having seen [the completion of] her milking and other activities,
<s>Kalāvatī</s>, who had come after observing [everything],
then spoke near her,
filled with supreme delight.
The cowherd (<s>Gopāla</s>) too, to his own cow-shed,
together with <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>,
accompanied by <s>Kavyagīṣpati</s>, in the evening
entered [the sky] like the moon.
<s>Rāma</s> bore the appearance of the king of celestials,
surrounded by a row of white[-clad attendants],
[resembling] the row of <s>Kailāsa</s> peaks,
with the majesty of <s>Airāvata</s> (Indra's elephant) standing in their midst.
In the midst, <s>Acyuta</s> (the Infallible One), shining among the rows of white [cows],
standing all around, lowing,
he gave to the people [a sight like] a dark bee wandering
amidst the rows of fully-bloomed white lotuses.

children.text: hihī gaṅge! godāvari! śabali! kālindi! dhavale!
children.translated_text: 'Hihī <s>Gaṅge</s>! <s>Godāvari</s>! <s>Śabalī</s>! <s>Kālindī</s>! <s>Dhavalā</s>!

children.text: hihī dhūmre! tūṅgi! bhramari! yamune! haṃsi! kamale!
children.translated_text: Hihī <s>Dhūmrā</s>! <s>Tūṅgī</s>! <s>Bhramarī</s>! <s>Yamunā</s>! <s>Haṃsī</s>! <s>Kamalā</s>!

children.text: hihī rambhe! campe! kariṇi! hariṇīti vraja-vidhur
children.translated_text: Hihī <s>Rambhā</s>! <s>Campā</s>! <s>Kariṇī</s>! <s>Hariṇī</s>!' — thus the lord of <s>Vraja</s>,
repeatedly calling them by name, summoned all the cows.
His body resting upon his toes, pressing the milking-pail against both knees,

children.text: kāścid dogdhi payaḥ svayaṃ tv atha parāḥ svair dohayaty unmukhīḥ
children.translated_text: some he milked himself, while others, eager-faced, he had milked by others.
Still others he fed to their own groups of calves, pleasing them with scratching —

children.text: itthaṃ nanda-sutaḥ prage svasurabhīr ānandayan nandati
children.translated_text: thus the son of <s>Nanda</s>, at dawn, delighting his own cows, rejoiced.
With sandals placed at the tips of his feet, heels gleaming with the delight of the three-points,

children.text: madhye nyasya ghaṭīṃ pa onnam anataḥ prodyat tviṣor jānunoḥ
children.translated_text: placing the pot in between, bending forward, radiance arising from both knees,
his turban slightly loosened from the beautiful contact with the cow's round [belly],

children.text: pāṇibhyāṃ krama-kuḍmalāṅguli-pu aṃ gāṃ dogdhi dugdhaṃ hariḥ
children.translated_text: with both hands, fingers gradually curling into buds, <s>Hari</s> milks the cow's milk.
Dearer even than her calf, through the touch of the Lord's lotus-hands —
the cow being milked herself, her udder overflowing with milk streaming from affection,
filling the milking-pail to the brim with streams of deep, resonant sound,

children.text: dohany antaram eti yāvad avanīṃ tāvat samāpupluvat
children.translated_text: in the interval between milkings, she overflowed upon the earth.
His fingers controlled by the tip of his thumb, the ground half-blocked by his foot,
pressing the edge of the udder, [first] with two or three drops of milk before him,
the streams falling into the mouth of the pail held between his lowered knees —

children.text: dhārā-dhvāna-manoharaṃ sakhi! payo gāṃ dogdhi dāmodaraḥ
children.translated_text: with the charming sound of streaming [milk], O friend, <s>Dāmodara</s> milks the cow.
As she listened, overwhelmed by the intensity of her emotions,
having forgotten the act of bathing,
<s>Lavaṅga-mañjarī</s> immediately
called out, her mind agitated.
There, upon a golden, soft seat
covered with Chinese silk, she was seated.
Attendants skilled in service quickly
surrounded her, bearing offerings in their hands.
She removed the collection of ornaments
from the body of her own dear friend <s>Lalitā</s>, tenderly,
as if from a golden creeper, lovingly,
a gathering of clusters of buds and flowers.
Wiping with a fine piece of cloth, most excellent,
every limb marked with the battle-marks of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless, Kāmadeva),
having dressed her in the garment worn during the oil-massage at night,
she released the garment endowed with the most exquisite fragrance.
Drawing the charming veil gently from her head,
loosening the tresses, luxuriant at the top of her head,
with a jeweled comb, her bangles clinking,
a certain excellent maidservant lovingly and respectfully combed [her hair].
Having washed her pair of feet, [and] showing a mirror before her,
a certain one praised for her expertise in the arts,
with fragrant oil of beautiful reddish hue,
anointed the lotus-faced one with abundant affection.
From whichever limb the lovely cloth was removed,
seeing that [exposed limb], she felt modesty gradually.
Observing that her friend's limb had been anointed thus and thus,
she covered all of that [exposed part], breaking through her shyness.
Having anointed her, the companions, their hearts pure and delighted,
massaged her body from foot to head.
They performed the <s>udvartana</s> (body-scrub) with powders full of camphor,
fine powders of musk, saffron, and sandalwood.
Having rubbed her hair with various means,
with fragrant decoctions of pure <s>āmalakī</s> (gooseberry),
with graceful streams flowing from the spout of the ewer,
she sprinkled [her] with innate affection.
With water scented with camphor as befitting the occasion,
held in pitchers studded with various lord-gems,
gently presented from both sides by two [attendants],
the two poured water on her sides — the beautiful-faced one.
Wrapping the beautiful tresses tightly with a cloth,
squeezing out the abundant flowing water, draining it thoroughly,
again spreading [the hair], separating it with moving fingers,
again a certain one bound the cloth, having distributed [the hair].
One [wiped] the moon [-like] face, another the base of the throat, another
the ears — the blessed one wiped with a soft cloth.

children.text: vakṣo visāri katamā katamā ca pṛṣṭhaṃ
children.translated_text: One [wiped] the spreading chest, one the back,
and one the pair of arms — most excellent in beauty.
Wrapping with a dry cloth, the inner garment
that had to be removed, dripping with water, she drew away from the hips.
Gently wiping with both hands, nobly,
she fastened the half-length garment at the edge of the waist.
Over the wiped, excellent breasts, without swaying,
a certain one skilled in the arts then bound the bodice.
With a silk garment fashioned by her own companion-women,
who were most adept in various extraordinary crafts,
over that, a delicate, redder [garment], from which arose
leaping, beautiful rays surpassing [those of] a fine silk canopy,
kissing the tips of the moon-like nail-rays of her blessed lotus-feet —
she bound that garment, connected with golden threads.
With a fine silk cord of two hanging, dangling [ends],
resplendent with the brilliance of pearls and the best gems,
through the sequence of gathering [the cloth], resembling a lotus,
she tied the <s>nīvi</s> (waist-knot) near the navel — a masterpiece of fine craft.
A new girdle-chain with golden dots,
brilliant in luster, shone forth upon it,
whose very encirclement is said to be
the restraint of <s>Mukunda's</s> (Kṛṣṇa's) unrestrained gaze.
Then, having placed her upon the back of a great jeweled seat,
established upon a spread of exceedingly soft cloth,
having washed her pair of lotus-feet with satisfaction,
her companions applied various auspicious attire and ornaments.
Again spreading and combing many times over,
purifying with fingers holding arrays of jeweled combs,
infusing [the hair] with the smoke of incense born of black <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood),
the group of companions made her mass of hair fragrant.
Having straightened the lovely locks [wet] from the bath into curls,
having drawn a <s>tilaka</s> (forehead mark) on the forehead with musk,
she placed a beautiful dot of <s>sindūra</s> (vermilion) on the hair-parting,
at the boundary of the <s>sīmanta</s> (parting), resplendent with the rays of the finest gems.
On both sides of the cheeks, a collection of <s>kastūrī</s> (musk) leaf-creeper designs;
on the forehead, surrounded on all sides by drops of <s>śrīkhaṇḍa</s> (sandal-paste), the design called <s>kāma-yantra</s> (love-diagram);
within, a crescent of musk-infused Malayan sandalwood drawn below —
she fashioned the <s>tilaka</s> adorned with the parting-line, with thick <s>sindūra</s> paste.
Upon the crown, a certain one bound the finest gem-crest,
bathed in the radiance of the inner hearts of <s>mālatī</s> flowers,
the <s>dhammilla</s> (braided hair-knot) with a gleaming red silk cord,
with two hanging, dangling [ornaments] of the finest gem-brilliance.
Through a fine golden pin inserted into the upper hole,
graceful at the junction of base and tip, she fashioned a beautiful one —
the blessed <s>cakrikā</s> (disc-ornament) and <s>bakulikā</s> (bakula-ornament) in the middle of the ear,
instructed by the weight of gem-radiance.
With an arrangement of pearl-strings, to be displayed by <s>Lalitā</s>,
a certain one placed a <s>patrapāśyā</s> (leaf-shaped ornament) at the border of the locks.
A certain one fitted the magnificent earrings of the finest gems,
one by one, to the pair of ears.
A certain one, having adorned the eyes with <s>añjana</s> (collyrium),
like the arrows of <s>Smāra</s> (Kāmadeva), polished with liquid <s>rasāñjana</s> (antimony),
placed a pearl on the left side of the nose,
blue-and-red with the splendor of collyrium and the beauty of the lower lip.
As she drew the <s>makarikā</s> (fish-shaped ornament) on both soft cheeks,
she was indeed summoning <s>Makara-ketana</s> (Kāmadeva, whose banner bears the crocodile),
to whom, offering the reddish shoot of her lower lip,
<s>Hari</s> would worship at the time of savoring.
In the middle of her lovely chin, with a jewel-radiant pin
held by the spread fingers of her hand, there shines
a dot of fresh musk, beautifying the blessed moon of her face —
like a bee settled upon the tip of a petal of a lotus.
With camphor, <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood), Kashmiri [saffron],
and paste mixed with sandalwood,
<s>Viśākhā</s> anointed
her back, arms, breasts, and chest.
A flower-cluster, crescent-moon-mark, lotus,
<s>makarī</s> (crocodile design), mango-shoot —
the talented <s>Citrā</s> painted wonderful [designs] with musk
on the surface of her breasts.
A <s>mīnī</s> (fish), a flower, a fresh shoot, a crescent-moon —
under the pretext [of these], <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) [hid] his own insignia: arrow, spear, and bow.
His power destroyed merely by the twang of the bow of her eyebrow —
I think he deposited [them] in the treasure-house of her breasts.
A bodice set with various, wonderful gems
and inlaid with pearls, of red silk,
wonderfully [decorated] with rainbow-like jewel-nets,
spread over her breasts like twilight-glow over mountains.
With nets of various gems set upon it, gleaming,
with a brilliant pure gold leaf-[design], <s>Viśākhā</s> [adorned] her throat —
of the lotus-eyed one — stealing the beauty of the mark of <s>Hari's</s> hand-pressure,
she immediately covered [it] in the middle, as if out of fear of <s>Hari</s>.
Studded with diamonds, decorated with various <s>Indra</s>-gems,
with a very thick middle, its beak bound with threads,
there gleamed at the pit of her throat
the wonderful swan of the necklace, given by her — [a] painted swan.
Glistening amid pairs of golden beads,
with <s>masāra</s> (emerald) beads interspersed,
strung with a very fine pearl-string by her —
a necklace called <s>gostana</s> ('cow-teat') was joined to her heart.
With interstices woven of <s>masāra</s> (emerald), moonstone, <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby),
and golden beads,
she attached a gem-garland strung with
pearls and coral upon her heart.
A <s>vaidūrya</s> (cat's-eye gem) pair set in a golden casket-like
bead-and-jewel [setting], with gems interspersed,
a wonderful cluster strung with variegated pearl-strings —
shone upon her heart, placed by her.
Given by <s>Hari</s> himself from his own neck during the <s>rāsa</s> (dance) at midnight,
pleased by the dancing and singing together,
like the very royal splendor itself [of that moment] —
she placed upon her heart the <s>guñjā</s> (rosary-bead) garland.
Lovely with thick rows of stars,
adorned with a fine central gem,
her <s>ekāvalī</s> (single-strand necklace), like moonlight,
decorated the sky of her heart.
With diamonds set in gold, encircled by <s>padmarāga</s> (rubies),
studded with <s>harimaṇi</s> (green gems), full within, of purest gold,
hanging from a delicate, brilliant chain of gold,
there gleamed upon her heart the four-piece [ornament] fitted by <s>Viśākhā</s>.
While being adorned by her companion-women at the time of the ornamentation-play,
the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>,
upon [receiving] the necklace of the finest blue gems placed upon her chest,
perspired, trembled, and was overcome with horripilation.
At the back, gradually hanging, a pure chain of necklaces trailing from the neck,
with a silk cord binding the waves, and a network of <s>camarī</s> (yak-tail fans) — upon her it shone.
I think it was clearly a staircase made by Providence with compassion

children.text: sopānaṃ vidhinā kṛtaṃ karuṇayā veṇī-bhujaṅgyāḥ sphuṭam
children.translated_text: for the serpent-like braid to ascend the summit of the beautiful mountain of her buttocks.
On the upper arms, incomparable armlets with fine gems;
on the forearms, incomparable bangles;
at their boundary, a certain one placed an auspicious silk-thread,
gleaming with gems, exceedingly wonderful with the luster of jewel-clasps.
With pearl-studded golden bracelets on both sides,
surrounded by an arrangement of bangles,
like the discs of the moon meeting the orb of the sun —
upon her it shone forth supremely, like <s>Rāhu</s> (the seizer of luminaries).
Engraved with her own name, interspersed
with the radiance of various gems,
her finger-rings shone —
crushers of the pride of rivals.
A jewel-crafted belly-band at the edge of the navel,
a girdle-string below it, with a binding of clusters of gems,
on the toes, a row of fine jeweled toe-rings,
up to the ankles, her companion fitted a pair of lovely anklets.
The nails, soles, and other [parts] of the feet, though possessing abundant redness,
ah! were further reddened with <s>yāvaka</s> (lac-dye).
'Is it possible, with a faint lamp-flame,
to augment the light of the sun created not by men?'
Another certain one said:
'In vain have you applied <s>yāvaka</s> to these lotus-feet;
their own redness is the elixir of the eyes.
But there is one quality of this [lac-dye], O <s>Rādhikā</s>:
it also colors the hair of <s>Keśava</s>.'
A pair of anklets, perfected with most lovely gems,
a certain one placed and fastened upon her lotus-feet.
To demonstrate her own expertise in craft,
one brought before her a mirror of the finest gems.
At dawn, <s>Viśākhā</s> placed upon her, brought by her own companion <s>Narmadā</s>,
a garland fashioned [by her].
Then, a lotus in the lotus-hand of [<s>Rādhā</s>] whose face was a smiling lotus,
a playful lotus for the lotus-eyed one —
she, seeing in the mirror her own reflected form and attire
suitable for delighting <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> eyes,
was restless with eagerness for <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> proximity — for noble women,
the fruit of special adornment is indeed the beloved's gaze.
His wrestling play and other [sports],
in their midst, together with his friends —
seeing [this], the golden-limbed one [<s>Rādhā</s>]
spoke quickly to her [friend] who had come [with the news].
Then, ceasing from the milking of cows, with his companions of charming pastimes,
together with his own dear friends of equal temperament,
he approached the jeweled hall for the daily practice
of playful wrestling sports, with single-minded devotion of all.
With each of these friends individually, of the same age, fearless,
he then engaged in wrestling, arm against arm,
displaying their respective strengths, with angry pride,
with retreating, creeping, advancing, and serpentine movements.
Resting a little, then with those [friends] — accumulated masses of merit,
roots of the great tree of virtues —
with charming smiles of delight for the purpose of oil-anointing,
he entered the auspicious anointing-house with his servants.
By those skilled in various compositions and many kinds of binding techniques,
enchanting in the special arts of auspicious oil-anointing,
with oil — a good, fragrant, noble companion —

children.text: prārambhi yat tad urarīkṛtam apy anena
children.translated_text: what was begun was indeed undertaken by him.
From foot to head, by those of undiminished complete fortune,
with oil, by those worthy of being honored in the beloved's assembly,

children.text: nātiślathaṃ ca na dṛḍhaṃ ca sumaṅgalāni
children.translated_text: neither too loosely nor too firmly, auspiciously,
they lovingly massaged those limbs of his for a long time.
They, with saffron powder, camphor granules,
full and beautifully soft, ground to a fine paste,
removing the oily residue thus produced,
rubbed those limbs of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
With some [water], fragrant with camphor,
held in vessels of various crystal and gold,
arranging his hair washed with herbal decoction, the group of young
maidservants bathed the lotus-eyed one.
One repeatedly combed the hair washed with decoction;
another gently wiped the soft limbs;
one sprinkled water from a ewer —
each surpassed the other in the beauty of devoted love.

children.text: jyotsnābhir nava-nīradaḥ kim athavā śuklena nīlo guṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Is it a new rain-cloud [adorned] with moonbeams? Or is it a dark cloth with a white thread?
Is it a sapphire sprout [bathed] in waters of pure crystal-gem luster?

children.text: muktābhiḥ kim u vā tamāla-taruṇaḥ snātaḥ samudbhrājate
children.translated_text: Or does a young <s>tamāla</s> tree bathed with pearls shine forth?

children.text: kiṃ vā śyāma-sarojam ujjvala-vidhukṣodair murārer vapuḥ
children.translated_text: Or is it <s>Murāri's</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>) body — a dark lotus [washed] with brilliant moon-drops?
Thus, some having completed the auspicious bathing
with conch-water poured upon his head,
bringing many body-wiping cloths,
they performed the drying, having humbly attended him.
First with soft, damp pieces of fine cloth,
then gradually they dried with white, fine, dry [cloths],
from foot to the mass of hair, at every joint and junction,
they performed the drying with loving devotion.
One skillfully arranged the water-free hair
with a twofold piece of cloth, with a gentle, soft smile;

children.text: kaścit paṭuḥ kaṭita ād galad ambu-celaṃ
children.translated_text: one expertly, with playful ease, removed the dripping wet cloth
from the waist with another cloth.
A new pair of silk garments, golden-yellow in hue,
brought swiftly by someone,
placed gradually in his lotus-hands by another —
removing the former cloth, he quickly put them on.
As he sat on a beautiful jeweled four-legged seat,
his lotus-feet washed, his body radiant,
a certain skilled young servant from behind
attended to the mass of his hair, expert in the task.
Spreading it out again, wiping it repeatedly, arranging it well,
purifying it many times with a jeweled comb,
covering [it] with a piece of cloth, that mass of hair,
tied in two sections, shone with radiance.
By the mutual comparison of the dark luster of the hair
and the whiteness of the exceedingly fine garment,
this arrangement of his hair, resembling a snake shedding its skin, the supreme enjoyer —

children.text: vinyāsa eṣa na hi kasya dṛśor viveśa
children.translated_text: indeed, whose eyes did it not enter?
Then, curling the locks straightened by bathing,
and coloring even the naturally curly ones,
on his forehead he drew a <s>tilaka</s> (sacred mark) resembling the moon's orb,
beautiful with the paste of sandalwood and saffron.
The emerald, sapphire, diamond, and ruby
that illuminate, as if making even the sinless radiate,
dense with rays that war against the splendor of others —
he placed the great king of jewels called <s>Śrī Kaustubha</s>.
He wore necklaces made of large pearl clusters,
which had attained a beauty beyond the reach of words —
one on his broad chest, one at the navel region,
one hanging low, and another at the base of the knees.
The <s>Śrī Kuṇḍalas</s> (sacred earrings), jeweled, shaped like <s>makara</s> (sea-creatures),
spreading the glory of luster upon his cheeks,
he brought to his blessed ears — [earrings] previously established [there],
which had been removed for the festive bathing.
Beautiful pendant ornaments made of fine silk threads,
touching the auspicious thread of gem-studded strands,
armlets made of emerald and the nine [types of] gems —
someone tied bracelets at the jeweled wrist-joints.
A divine ring, magnificent, on the ring-finger,
which was the culmination of the radiance of its ruby —
and an irresistible jeweled signet-ring on the back [of the hand],
someone placed on the forefinger, a delightful [sight].
Connected with an assemblage of various chief jewels,
a waist-band around the interior of the yellow garment,
with strings of ruby bells at the base of the girdle —
someone tied [these] on the resplendent silk cloth worn [by him].
Upon the lotus-feet, fashioned with chief jewels,
a pair of anklets, bright with moon-like [radiance of] nails,
placing a most magnificent jeweled mirror,
someone eagerly held it before his moon-like face.
Meanwhile, someone, carrying the command

children.text: ādāya kaścana tad asya gṛhaṃ viveśa
children.translated_text: of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> [<s>Nanda</s>], entered his [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>] house

children.text: ūce ca kṛṣṇa! janakasya girā bahubhyas
children.translated_text: and said: 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! By your father's word,

children.text: tvaṃ dātum arhasi gavām ayutaṃ dvijebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: you should give ten thousand cows to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> out of the many.'

children.text: śrutvā pitur giram asau cikuraṃ nibadhya
children.translated_text: Hearing his father's word, he tied his hair
and properly arranged his yellow upper garment;
sipping water [for purification], with a lovely face, [he who is] a peak of the mountain of virtuous gems,
the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>, with a devoted mind, distributed the cows.
While the flavorful cooking most desired by the queen of the cowherds [<s>Yaśodā</s>]
was being prepared, consisting of many courses,
unable to endure the delay until then,

children.text: sā prāhiṇot kim api bhoktum athāvilambam
children.translated_text: she sent something for him to eat immediately.
Food of fresh butter, yogurt, milk, cream, and other delicacies,
spiced with camphor powder —
having sipped water [for purification], leaning on the shoulder of his dear friend,
he took betel — [he whose face is] a sweet moon-disc.
Hearing this news, sweet as nectar, delighted,

children.text: svayaṃ paktvā yan no tad-aśanam asau kāritavatī
children.translated_text: [<s>Rādhā</s>], that he himself had eaten what she had cooked for them —
overcome [with emotion], from her eyes she released
a shower of teardrops like frost and dew from a pair of lotuses.
Meanwhile, by the queen of <s>Vraja</s> [<s>Yaśodā</s>], the unfailing
creeper of maternal affection, most joyfully directed,
coming, <s>Kundavalatī</s>, with a radiant beauty, to delight
the bee-like eyes [of <s>Rādhā</s>], shone forth accomplished.
A rain of nectar [arising] from the mutual seeing, the arising smiles,
the eagerness of beloved conversation, the rising of delight —

children.text: sadyo babhūva yata eva tadā tad-āli-
children.translated_text: occurred at once, whereby then that group
of her friends rejoiced, their hearts [glowing] with equal friendship.
'The grace of the supreme queen of <s>Vraja</s>

children.text: mayi sakhi! vyakti tavodayo hy akasmāt
children.translated_text: upon me, O friend, your sudden arrival indeed reveals;
without the moon, in the eastern

children.text: diśam adhi rātri sameti kāpi lakṣmīḥ
children.translated_text: direction at night there comes no splendor.'
'Therefore I infer that out of the pretense of command,

children.text: kim api kṛpāmṛtam eva sā vyatārīt
children.translated_text: she has bestowed some nectar of compassion,
for, not having perceived this, my self
considers even itself as not its own, with sorrow.'
'You were born for the purpose of creating delicious [food],

children.text: rasavati! te gatir ity avaimi nūnam
children.translated_text: O flavorful one! That your destiny is thus, I know for certain;
otherwise why else would you have come so swiftly,
first pleasing this revered lady of mine?'
Drinking the nectar of the beautiful-eyed one's words,
<s>Kundavallī</s> spoke with a lovely smile:

children.text: tad ayi sakhi! vidhehi tatra yātrām
children.translated_text: 'Then, O friend, make the journey there
without delay, together with the group of friends;
in the matter of obtaining the permission of the elders,
is there even the slightest difficulty?'
'She who by showers of incomparable wealth, cows, and grain

children.text: akṛta vaśāṃ svayam eva tāṃ vrajeśā
children.translated_text: has herself brought the queen of <s>Vraja</s> under her sway —
the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> is the unconditional, supreme beloved
of all people dwelling in the cowherd settlement, more than their own lives;
what he desires
here, who can have any objection to it?'

children.text: sakhi! kim api na veda tat savitrī
children.translated_text: 'O friend! Even <s>Sāvitrī</s> [the sun-deity's wife] does not know that,
that incomparably delightful substance, which you wish to prepare;
proper or improper, one's own gain or loss,
distinction between one's own and another's, fame or infamy —

children.text: pacasi yad api yaś ca tasya bhoktā
children.translated_text: [none of this matters] for what you cook and for him who eats it,

children.text: sa ca tirayaty amṛtaṃ sadaiva divyam
children.translated_text: for he always surpasses even divine nectar.'
'Thus, this fame of yours, well-known in all settlements,

children.text: tava sakhi! kaṃ na camatkaroti bāḍham
children.translated_text: O friend! Whom does it not truly astonish?'

children.text: yad avadhi kalayāṃ babhūva sā tvāṃ
children.translated_text: 'From the time she [<s>Yaśodā</s>] came to know you
as the one blessed by the best of sages, O beautiful lotus-eyed one!
From that time, not even on a single day has she caused
a cessation of eating food prepared by your hands.'
'He who conquers the most terrible hordes of demons,
though of tender body, desiring the welfare of his own and others —
other than the eating of food cooked by your pure hands,

children.text: aparam iyaṃ manute na hetum atra
children.translated_text: he considers no other cause for this [his strength].'
'Listen, O supreme <s>Rādhā</s>, to the truth in this matter:
what I have suddenly learned of her [<s>Yaśodā's</s>] inner [feelings] —
without seeing you daily,
O moon-faced one! She grieves as [she would] for her own son.'
The beautiful-bodied one [<s>Rādhā</s>] said: 'Take note, O wise one!

children.text: sakhi! tad idaṃ na vadasy ayuktam ittham
children.translated_text: O friend! Do not speak thus inappropriately;
for those who claim [her to be] of noble family,
it is clearly improper [to say she is] led to another's woman.'

children.text: yad api bata sakhīyaṃ rītir eveha loke
children.translated_text: 'Even though this is indeed the custom among friends in this world,

children.text: tad api tava vaco no laṅghanīyaṃ kadāpi
children.translated_text: still, your words must never be transgressed;

children.text: anunaya prathamaṃ tāṃ kintu yuktyā hi vṛddhāṃ
children.translated_text: but first, skillfully pacify that old woman

children.text: parivadati tu yā mām āśu labdhvāpi rāyam
children.translated_text: who reproaches me, even after having obtained wealth.'
Then, approaching <s>Jaṭilā</s>,
though [she was] crooked toward her daughter-in-law,
the clever one conveyed the message
of the queen of <s>Vraja</s>.
Hearing the command of the queen of the cowherd king,
[<s>Jaṭilā</s>], though suspicious of her daughter-in-law because of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
reflecting on the instruction of <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>,
spoke to <s>Kundavallī</s> with affection:
'This daughter-in-law of mine is virtuous, sweet as the honey of the weight of virtues;

children.text: janaś chidrānveṣī sa khalu capalo nanda-tanayaḥ
children.translated_text: but that restless son of <s>Nanda</s> is indeed a seeker of faults in others;
nor should the command of the queen of the cowherd lord be disregarded, nor the words of the venerable

children.text: vacaḥ pālyaṃ vatse! na ati hṛdayaṃ kiṃ nu karavai!
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> — it must be obeyed, O child! Does it not tear the heart! What can I do?'

children.text: mātaḥ! satyaṃ vadati bhavatī kiṃca gopendra-sūnur
children.translated_text: 'Mother! What you say is true; however, the son of the chief of cowherds
should not be known as what the wicked crowds have proclaimed him to be,
but rather, like the rising sun toward the lotus of true dharma, [while] toward the owl-row of the wicked
and toward the darkness of sin — he is [like] the <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy goose) of the cowherd settlement's delight.'
'His sweetness, however, intoxicates the young women of the world; therefore

children.text: bhītir nītis tava nava-vadhū-pālanaṃ cāpi yuktam
children.translated_text: your fear and your policy of guarding the new bride are also justified;

children.text: māśaṅkiṣṭhās tad ayati yathā dṛk-pathaṃ nāsya sādhvyāś
children.translated_text: do not worry — I shall ensure that not even the shadow of this virtuous lady

children.text: chāyāpy asyāḥ svayam aham imāṃ drāk tathā te'rpayāmi
children.translated_text: falls in his line of sight; I myself shall quickly deliver her to you thus.'
'You, O daughter, are known as virtuous in the settlement;
to you is entrusted this innocent bride, therefore
that roving-eyed son of <s>Nanda</s> —
see to it that he does not look upon her.'
Then, summoning the bride, she said: 'O child,
go to the house of <s>Nanda's</s> bride [<s>Yaśodā</s>] in the cowherd settlement,
accomplish what is dear to her and come back quickly;
together with these [companions], the sun is to be worshipped by you today.'
Though <s>Rādhā</s> was thus directed and inwardly delighted,

children.text: py anicchuvad gantum uvāca tāṃ sakhīm
children.translated_text: as if unwilling to go, she said to that friend:

children.text: astīha kṛtyaṃ na ca me yiyāsutā
children.translated_text: 'There is duty for me here, and I have no desire to go —'
that she does not move from house to house among the family women —
the words of the wife of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, long entreated
with humility and affection, rooted in supplication —
how many [of these requests] can we refuse here?
May the blessed Lord <s>Hari</s> Himself be your protector!
He protects this world and the guardians of <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: kim iha satīḥ sa jahāti lokanāthaḥ?
children.translated_text: would He, the Lord of the world, forsake virtuous women?
Thus, having placed you in His hand,
O beautiful-faced one! I would be free from worry.'
At these words of the venerable old woman, [<s>Rādhā</s>],
graceful with the suppression of a slight emerging smile, [looking at] her own friends
with a play of glances from the corners of her blooming dark eyes,

children.text: kim api nigadya babhūva sāpi tūṣṇīm
children.translated_text: having said something [inaudible], became silent.
Insistently urged again loudly by the elder,
by <s>Kaundī</s> (grandmother <s>Mukhara</s>), who pulled her hand, she spoke:

children.text: bhītāsi kiṃ sādhvy aham asmy avitrī-
children.translated_text: 'Are you afraid, O virtuous one? I am the protectress!' —
thus lifted up, her body blossoming [with joy], she set forth.
For <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> morning meal,
prepared <s>laḍḍukas</s> and other [sweets],
carrying [these], <s>Lalitā</s> and the chief
<s>sakhīs</s> (friends) also followed their friend.
Then, as she emerged from her own dwelling,
with the splendor of her slender garments and ornaments,
she adorned the city-lane, jewel-studded and golden,
perfuming all directions.
In the coming and going of crowds of people,
slightly averting her face, keeping to one side of the road,
with downcast eyes, her lotus-face unspeaking,
she attained the sweetness of the all-enveloping veil.
Seeing on the road [<s>Rādhā</s>] with the cloth on her chest
moving with supreme bliss,
<s>Kundavallī</s>, together with her companion,
teased her lovingly.
'Your husband, having gone to fetch supplies for three or four days, returned at dusk

children.text: bhartā gobhiḥ svagoṣṭhe ghaṭayitum akhilāṃ rātrim eva nyavātsīt
children.translated_text: and spent the entire night in his own cowshed settling the cows;

children.text: vakṣaḥ prodyan nakhāṅkāvali-citam adharaḥ spaṣṭa-danta-kṣato yat
children.translated_text: yet your chest displays emerging rows of nail-marks, and your lip clearly shows tooth-bites —

children.text: tat sādhvyās te satītvaṃ samucitam adhunā vyaktam ullālasīti
children.translated_text: that being so, your chastity, O virtuous one, is now clearly manifest!' — thus she jested.
With a suppressed inner smile,
eyes slightly narrowed,
seeing her own friend <s>Kundavallī</s>,
<s>Lalitā</s> then spoke:
'A bold parrot in the garden, mistaking [her breast] for a <s>karaka</s>-fruit,
alighted upon her breast, and confusing [her lip] for a ripe <s>bimba</s>-fruit,

children.text: adaśad adharam uccais tan-nakhāco itaṃ tad-
children.translated_text: bit her lip fiercely — those nail-marks are from that,

children.text: dhṛdayam idam amuṣyāḥ kiṃ vṛthā śaṅkase tvam
children.translated_text: and this is [the mark on] her heart — why do you suspect in vain?'
Seeing her [<s>Rādhā</s>], her body trembling with waves of agitation
from the memory of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> love-play, recalled by the friend's words,
gazing at a lotus-lake,
<s>KundaLatā</s> sang again, laughing:
'You tremble with waves of bliss, O innocent one!
Why in vain [do you look], O <s>Padminī</s> (lotus-woman)? — of <s>Kundavallī's</s> [words],
will not that brother-in-law of yours, <s>Madhusūdana</s>,
wandering again, drink you who are already enjoyed and released?'
A witty play-on-words delightful to the ear,
an ornament like earrings —
'Ah, what a deed!' — to that <s>Kundavallī</s>,
the discerning <s>Viśākhā</s> said:
'Though herself bearing supreme love,
though blooming and tender, [she trembles] before the very fickle bee —
this good lotus-woman, O friend <s>Kundavallī</s>,
trembles in fear of the bee's younger brother.'
Then next —
'Sometimes on a deserted path,
when she walks clearly [engaged] in the sport of mutual conversation,

children.text: yadi calati tadā kutaḥ kva yāmī-
children.translated_text: then, "where am I going?" —
she does not even make [the path] an object of perception.'
'Her mind bewildered by love for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
generating a mass of bliss —
<s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> showed her, walking on the path,
<s>Nandīśvara</s> (Nanda's palace-hill) indeed.'
With <s>rasāla</s> (mango), <s>panasa</s> (jackfruit), <s>arjuna</s>, <s>kramuka</s> (betel-palm), and coconut trees,
with <s>palāśa</s>, <s>vaṭa</s> (banyan), <s>parkaṭī</s> (fig), <s>khadira</s> (acacia), <s>bilva</s>, <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple) and others,
with <s>madhūka</s>, <s>girimallikā</s>, <s>bakula</s>, <s>nāga</s> (nāgakeśara), and <s>punnāga</s> trees,
with <s>aśoka</s>, <s>baka</s>, <s>pāṭalī</s>, golden <s>campakas</s> and <s>campakas</s>,
with <s>tamāla</s>, <s>navamālikā</s>, golden <s>yūthikā</s>, <s>yūthikā</s> (jasmine),
<s>kuraṇḍaka</s>, <s>lavaṅgikā</s> (clove-vine), <s>damanaka</s>, <s>atimuktā</s> and others,
also with land-lotuses, <s>vicakilā</s> and others, <s>kandalī</s> (banana),
<s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>tulasī</s> (holy basil) and other variegated creepers and plants,
with white, dark, and red <s>utpalas</s> (lotuses), day-lotuses, and <s>kahlāras</s> (white lilies),
with <s>cakravākas</s> (ruddy geese), herons, <s>sārasas</s> (cranes), <s>kuraras</s> (ospreys), swans, and <s>kāraṇḍavas</s> (ducks),
adorned with waves, with pure waters, with ponds,
tanks, lakes, and other water-bodies surrounding [them] —
with the lowing of cows here, and of the cowherds
the clamor of various skilled minstrels —
it shines with the love of the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>,
[<s>Nandīśvara</s>], greater even than <s>Govardhana</s>, worshipped by <s>Vraja</s>.
'O friend! Not far before you has appeared
the dwelling of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, situated nearby;
so now, the longing of your <s>cātaka</s>-bird-like eyes
is about to bear fruit — believe this!'
At those very words of her friend,
her body instantly overcome with trembling and numbness,
<s>Kaundī</s> forcibly supported her, reviving her,

children.text: kim api jagāda ca tāṃ tadaiva kaundī
children.translated_text: and said something to her at that moment:
'O beautiful-faced one! Why have you become agitated just now,
when <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s> has not yet come within the range of your eyes?
Your complete chastity is well-known —

children.text: tava savayaḥ sada eva yat pramāṇam
children.translated_text: your own age-mates are always the proof of that.

children.text: dhṛtim iha hṛdi dhartum īśiṣe no
children.translated_text: Though you cannot hold composure here in your heart,

children.text: yad api tad apy abale! kṣaṇaṃ dadhīthāḥ
children.translated_text: O delicate one! At least maintain it for a moment;
for bearing the weight of twin mountains [your breasts],
I must today engage <s>Giridhari</s> (the mountain-lifter) for you.'
'Because of [the mention of] the direction of <s>Giridhari</s>, she who
became distressed today — this friend is a great chaste woman!
You forcibly tease this unknowing one!

children.text: tad api niyokṣyasi hā punas tam asyām
children.translated_text: And yet you will again assign him to her!
That you have repeatedly entrusted her to the elder [Yaśodā] —
what you now wish to accomplish is indeed proper, O blessed one!'

children.text: svam iva sakhi! paraṃ janaṃ na viddhī-
children.translated_text: 'Do not regard another person as you would your own, O friend!' —
having said this, <s>Lalitā</s> spoke again to those two:
'Enough, enough of this talk! Look! Nearby,
before [us], near the gate-arch,
[see] the courtyard paved with crystal studded with gems,
freshly laid — the one desire of the heart!'
'Having playfully milked at dawn,
together with companions, having played wrestling-games,
having heard the news of your group's arrival,
He has come, His heart agitated — look, He shines!'
'Enveloped by the brilliant circle of beauty
capable of intoxicating the women-folk of <s>Vraja</s>,
bearing the weight of sweetness itself — why the <s>tribhaṅgī</s> (triple-bend)
pose of His body, with swaying garlands, having captivated the row of friends?
His pair of eyes, adorned with earrings resting on the softest cheeks,
expert in the supreme dance of loving glances,
with waves of golden and dark radiance from His garments fluttering in the breeze,
having stilled all directions,
His left arm, whose splendor mocks a rising elephant's trunk,
resting on the shoulder of His dear friend,
His other hand, with the sole passion of twirling
a lotus surpassed by His own radiance — He presides!'
Then, if she [<s>Rādhā</s>], having made her ears and eyes into cups,
[drank in] those words and that beauty's sweetness —
even if not, then that [fragrance] from His direction,
the spreading perfume, quickly awakened her.
Though overwhelmed with horripilation, trembling, abundant tears,
and perspiration, [yet] maintaining composure, she said:

children.text: sakhi! kim aparam asti vartma pādau
children.translated_text: 'O friend! Is there another path? My feet

children.text: na mama puraś calato 'sya kiṃ karomi
children.translated_text: do not move forward before Him — what shall I do?'
'The control of elders itself is expert

children.text: karaṇa-paṭus tava kiṃ bhiyā hriyā vā
children.translated_text: in removing faults for you — why fear or be ashamed?'
Thus encouraged by her companion,

children.text: laghu laghu gantum iyeṣa sā tad agre
children.translated_text: she desired to go quickly, quickly, before him.
'What is this?' — under the pretext of mutual glances,
in that supremely sweet [exchange] between those two — those [friends]
drowned themselves in their own incomparable [bliss] —

children.text: laya iti varṇayituṃ na gīr apīṣṭe
children.translated_text: even speech does not wish to describe [it] to the point of dissolution.
Those moonbeams of the <s>cakora</s>-bird <s>Aghadamana</s> (Kṛṣṇa, destroyer of Agha) —
the moon-faced one drank them again and again, ever thirsting;
and like a <s>cātaka</s>-bird above the cloud that is <s>Giridhari</s>,
she rained abundant <s>rasa</s> (love) — thus, how wondrous!
Then, placing their left hands upon their respective heads
with the artful gesture of adjusting their veils, those [women],
their downcast eyelid-edges drinking
the nectar of the beloved's lotus-feet, departed from before Him.
<s>Hari</s> too, turning around, stood
with His lotus-eyes fixed on the radiance of their hips;
and the row of beautiful women, having passed beyond His
cow-village, slightly loosened their veils.
'O friend! He, delighted at the sight of you,
instantly made that young student happy
with a <s>campaka</s>-garland — being a knower of gestures,

children.text: bhavasi na vety uditāha sā svasakhyā
children.translated_text: are you or are you not?' — so said her friend to her.
'You are just as you were — you fixed
your own eyes, wishing to make them [reach] another' —
thus, with a slightly blossoming smile, with moving brows,
she quickly reached the interior of the great city.
With crystal-built walls, admirable and magnificent,
blazing with thresholds, bolted with diamond-pins,
with rows of gem-studded statues of women holding lamps,
adorned with rows of trees and birds at the doors,
with gem-filled pitchers blazing in the sun's rays,
with flags, banners, and peacocks adorning the front courtyards,
where surpassing the city of the chief of gods,
there shines the cluster of mansions, rich with <s>Indirā</s> (Lakṣmī),
with sapphire ramparts, emerald chambers, golden thresholds,
with rows of coral pillars, crystal floors, and <s>vaidūrya</s> (cat's-eye) beams,
with great sapphire portals, pure <s>kuruvinda</s>-ruby
gatekeepers — the city whose varied forms surpass rows of celestial chariots.
On the wall, fashioned with finest gems by artistic craftsmanship,
parrots [depicted] alongside the household parrots who have settled [nearby] —

children.text: saprāṇāḥ kim amī ime kim atha vety unmīlataḥ saṃśayād-
children.translated_text: 'Are these alive or are those [the real ones]?' — from the doubt arising upon opening [their eyes],
the innocent women are long bewildered, [wondering whether] to offer pomegranate seeds.
In the main quadrangular courtyard of hers [<s>Yaśodā's</s>],
the treasure-house is in the western direction,
<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa's</s> quarters are in the auspicious south,
<s>Śrī Rāma's</s> (Balarāma's) abode rises in the northern direction.
In the east is a similar chamber, where
in the eastern [section] of one of its inner rooms,
for the welfare of his son, his chosen deity,
<s>Nanda</s> worships <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> indeed.
Adjoining the southern side of the treasury,
to the auspicious west of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> quarters,
between the two kitchens,
is the spacious resting-chamber of <s>Rādhikā</s>.
Adjoining the southern side of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> quarters,
the kitchen too stands resplendent;
there is a garden and a lake there,
a secluded, delightful [area] with many chambers and platforms.
Then, as she [<s>Rādhā</s>] arrived with her friends, illuminating
<s>Hari's</s> mother's own dwelling,
[<s>Yaśodā</s>] regarded her as the sole wealth of the three worlds,
the risen daughter of <s>Arkamitra</s> (the Sun's friend, i.e., Kīrtidā) — delighted.
She [<s>Rādhā</s>] who had come there, prostrate at [<s>Yaśodā's</s>] feet, was lifted
by her arms; <s>Mukunda's</s> mother placed her in her heart,
smelling her head with joy, the supreme mother,
affectionately kissed her face, becoming tear-faced.
Embracing each of her companions too,
she asked after their unimpaired welfare;
eager to quickly arrange food for her son,
she addressed these [friends] again with affection:
'You are not the daughter of <s>Kīrtidā</s> [alone],
but truly mine alone — I declare this truthfully.
I live by seeing your face,
which is just like <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> — why are you bashful?'
Seating her together with sweet, soft <s>modakas</s> and other [refreshments]
along with the group of friends, by gentle force,
her heart melting, having <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> serve [them],
thoroughly pampering [them], she led [<s>Rādhā</s>] to the kitchen.
'You who have gained fame in producing various sweet delicacies,
renowned in the land of <s>Vraja</s> as having skilled hands for sweets —

children.text: tad iha kuruta putryaḥ! sādhu bhakṣyāṇi yatnād
children.translated_text: so here, O daughters, prepare fine delicacies with care,

children.text: dara-rucir api vatsaḥ saspṛhaṃ me yathātti
children.translated_text: so that my boy, though having little appetite, may eat eagerly!'
'Some of you make the salted [preparations],
some make the yogurt-based [dishes],
others [make] the ghee-based [sweets] —
O daughters, and others the sugar-based [confections]!'
'You are expert in the proper methods of flavorful preparations;

children.text: tvam iha rasavatīṃ me yāhi rādhe! prayatnāt
children.translated_text: O <s>Rādhe</s>! Go to my kitchen with special care!
O mother [<s>Rādhā</s>]! Prepare delicious rice under the supervision of the mother of <s>Bala</s> (Rohiṇī),
and together with her, make excellent side-dishes!'
'Prepare <s>vaṭaka</s> (fried savory) and <s>amṛta-keli</s> with greatest effort,
and another smooth, flavorful <s>karpūra-keli</s> (camphor-sweet), O daughter!
Sweet beyond tens of millions of nectars, for which <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is ever desirous —

children.text: trijagati na hi kaścit tvām ṛte yasya vettā
children.translated_text: in the three worlds, no one but you knows [how to make] it!
That for which my son has the greatest craving —
having also made the <s>pīyūṣa-granthi-pālī</s> (rows of nectar-knots, a sweet) —'
In the drink mixed with camphor, cardamom and such,
carefully, dear child, prepare what is called pañcāmṛta (five nectars)!
You, O <s>Lalitā</s>, mother, prepare the <s>rasālā</s> (flavored curd)!
And you, <s>Viśākhā</s>, quickly [prepare] the <s>ṣāḍava</s> (a sweet dish) here!
And you, O <s>Śaśilekhā</s>, [prepare] the <s>śikhariṇī</s> (a sweetened yogurt)!
Daughter <s>Campakalatā</s>, you [prepare] the <s>mathita</s> (churned drink)!
You, daughter, prepare the <s>āmikṣā</s> (curdled milk) of hers,
with the respective ingredients, in various methods of cooking and blending;
make the various kinds, O <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>!
You, mother <s>Citrā</s>, [prepare] the <s>matsyaṇḍī</s> drinks!
You, <s>Raṅgadevī</s>, [prepare] the <s>khaṇḍa-maṇḍa</s> (sugar confections)!
You, <s>Sudevī</s>, [prepare] various milk-essences!
<s>Vāsantī</s>, you [prepare] soft white <s>phenikā</s> (frothy sweets)!
You, <s>Maṅgalā</s>, prepare the <s>kuṇḍalikā</s> (spiral sweet)!
<s>Kādambarī</s>, you make the <s>candrakānti</s> (moonlight sweets)!
You, <s>Lāsikā</s>, [make] the balls of rice-flour!
You, <s>Kaumudī</s>, [prepare] <s>śaṣkulī</s> (pastries) of many varieties!
You, mother <s>Madālasā</s>, [prepare] the <s>indupiṇḍa</s> (moon-shaped sweets)!

children.text: śaśimukhi! va akāni tvaṃ vidhehi prayatnād
children.translated_text: O <s>Śaśimukhī</s> (moon-faced one)! Carefully prepare the <s>vaṭaka</s> (fritters),
curd-<s>vaṭaka</s> and such, brimming with abundant sweetness!

children.text: praṇaya sumukhi! ramyāḥ śarkarā-pa ikās tvaṃ
children.translated_text: With love, O <s>Sumukhī</s> (beautiful-faced one), you [prepare] lovely sugar <s>paṭikā</s> (candy)!
O <s>Maṇimatī</s>, you [prepare] <s>piṣṭānna-pūpa</s> (flour cakes) of many varieties!
Prepare, O dear child <s>Kāñcanavalī</s>,
<s>laḍḍuka</s> (sweet balls) made from wheat flour,
called <s>manoharā</s> (enchanting), O <s>Manoramā</s>!
And you, <s>Ratnamālā</s>, [make] those called <s>mauktika</s> (pearl-like)!
With well-husked, dehusked sesame seeds,
make <s>modaka</s> (sweetmeats), O <s>Mādhavī</s>!
Likewise those called <s>tila-kadamba</s> (sesame clusters),
sesame <s>khaṇḍa-paṭikā</s> (sugar-candy with sesame).
Puffed rice and parched grains, well-roasted,
flattened rice fried in ghee --
having prepared [these], O <s>Vindhyā</s>, with sugar-syrup,
make box-shaped <s>modaka</s> (sweetmeats)!
O <s>Rambhā</s>, prepare <s>karambha</s> (porridge) in a golden
vessel, with plantain fruits, sugar, and other [ingredients]!
Having squeezed ripe mango juice, O <s>Manojñā</s> (charming one),
prepare it mixed with sugar, thickened milk, and cream!
The curd that I churned and prepared
this morning from fragrant milk --
from that, [make] a lump of fragrant fresh butter,
<s>haiyaṅgavīna</s> (day-fresh butter) -- make it, O <s>Kilimbā</s>!
The milk of the white cow, milked personally
by the lord of <s>Vraja</s> and sent [here] --
for the drinking of the two boys, O <s>Ambikā</s>,
gently heat it!
Surrounded by rows of ladles and spoons,
with vessels of clay, wood, and pots,
rich with rows of hearths, sprinkled and plastered by me --
go quickly to that milk-kitchen, O girls!
The various utensils,
each and every one, O <s>Dhaniṣṭhikā</s>,
taking them out from those respective containers,
place them in dishes and have them distributed!
Those respective ingredients, quickly, together with <s>Tulasī</s>,
you, <s>Raṅgaṇamālikā</s>,
having brought from our storeroom,
have the groups of maidservants distribute them here and there!
<s>Āmrātaka</s> (hog-plum), mango, citron, <s>karīra</s> (caper), <s>dhātrī</s> (emblic myrobalan),
<s>limpāka</s>, <s>koli</s> (jujube), <s>rucaka</s> and other fruits in abundance,
long preserved indeed in oil with salt,
and roots such as fresh ginger, and appetizing [condiments] --
tamarind ripened and long-soaked in <s>matsyaṇḍikā</s> (raw sugar) juice,
likewise pieces of <s>dhātrī</s> (amla), <s>rasāla</s> (mango), and <s>badarī</s> (jujube),
taking them out from the pickle-jars, O you,
having prepared them, O moon-faced one, place them in golden vessels!
O auspicious <s>Śandā</s>, <s>Śubhā</s>, <s>Bharaṇī</s>, stout one, skilled of hand!
Upon the rows of hearths, on the unequalled churning vessels,
the milk brought by the carriers from the cowshed --
children, slowly heat it, placing it carefully, quickly!
Having eaten the remainder of her beloved's [meal],
having become joyful,
to her who had come near him,
he spoke to <s>Rādhā</s> with affection:
O lotus-faced one! O sole glory of <s>Kīrtidā</s>!
You have been made skillful in the art of cooking by the Creator;
therefore, entering the kitchen with relish,
complete the task begun by <s>Lalitā</s> and the other <s>sakhīs</s> (friends)!
O moon-faced one! May you triumph thus for a hundred autumns;
delight the eyes of my mind! -- having spoken thus,
the supremely charming one led her companions,
that creeper of incomparable maternal affection, bowing -- she [went].
Having saluted the queen of the cowherds with special humility,
her hand held in that one's lotus-palm, exceedingly lovely,
having reached and bowed to the mother of <s>Rāma</s> who had come,
she, of noble birth, assumed the supervision of the cooking work.
Bearing a luster like <s>Kailāsa</s> mountain in her own radiance,
wearing blue garments, the loving <s>Rādhā</s> always [shone] here;
repeatedly saying 'Come!' with the extension of her arms,
she embraced her with a kiss on the face, laughing.
Having entered the kitchen with those two, the young women

children.text: pālīḥ smitena mṛdunā vacasā ca bālā
children.translated_text: of the cooking hall,
honoring [them] with a gentle smile and soft words, she of praiseworthy conduct rejoiced
upon seeing those cooking implements, measured and arranged.
Pumpkin, <s>ālu</s> (potato), <s>kacu</s> (taro), <s>mānaka</s> (a root vegetable), tuber, bottle-gourd,
eggplant, radish, <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd) fruits, beans,
<s>ḍiṇḍīśa</s> (a gourd), <s>vāraṇa</s>, <s>buṣāma</s> fruits, <s>anīcā</s>,
special varieties of plantain, fresh cores, and tender banana blossoms,
<s>vāstūka</s> (chenopodium) greens, <s>māriṣa</s> (amaranth), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd) tips, pea
vine-tips, chickpea shoot-tips -- having spread out
tender bottle-gourd tips along with <s>podikā</s> (a leafy green) tops,
she looked upon all the juicy [vegetables], beholding her friends gathered together.

children.text: yad yena yena vidhinā ruciratvam etya
children.translated_text: Knowing by which method each [vegetable] attains deliciousness,

children.text: yad vyañjane yad upayujyata ity avetya
children.translated_text: and which is used in which curry -- having understood,
those things, by those kitchen-workers,
were then pounded and chopped in the respective manner.
Cardamom, clove, pepper, fresh ginger, nutmeg flower, <s>ajājī</s> (cumin),
nutmeg, cinnamon, <s>sulāṅgali</s>, rows of mustard seeds,
mustard grain, rice, turmeric, and split black gram --
some attendants ground all of these for the lotus-eyed ones.
Having ground [them] and placed in golden boxes, covered
with auspicious, radiant lids by the group of attendants,
well-arranged upon cloth, she of faultless character
set her heart upon the sport of cooking.
Resplendent with essential ornaments and attire,
with washed lotus-[like] feet and hands, together with <s>Rohiṇī</s>,
she shone upon the platform of the excellent kitchen,
with faith and curiosity in the act of cooking.
When the hearths blazed with fire at <s>Rāma's</s> mother's signal,
[with fire] from the most beautiful firewood, resplendent,
there ascended [onto them] the cooking vessels of copper, brass, and silver,
captivating the eyes and hearts of all.
The fire itself blazed, smokeless, without sputtering;
the fire itself became water -- [in] an unprecedented abundance.

children.text: yad yatra yatra lavaṇaṃ ca tathā pramāṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Whatever salt and measure [was needed] wherever,
that she made authoritative [merely] in the palm of her hand.
Upon the tops of the rows of hearths, enveloped
by the flames of <s>aguru</s> (aloe), <s>sarala</s> (pine), and <s>devadāru</s> (cedar) wood,
with rows of various vessels placed, shining,
for the proper preparation of the many kinds of tempering --
from the [activities of] managing the fire, holding vessels, lifting up
and setting down, stirring, ladle-turning and such,
due to the trembling of her triple-fold [waist], breasts, arms, and shoulders, and the fluttering of garments,
there arose then in her
a fullness of sweetness, which <s>Acyuta</s>, from his own palace,
through the shining lattice window, holding his gaze, drinking it in,
revealing the swelling intoxication of <s>Madana</s> (love),

children.text: kim api jagāda paṭur baṭuṃ miṣeṇa
children.translated_text: the clever one said something to a student (<s>baṭu</s>) as a pretext.
Having sent him, she then went to the kitchen:

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ tvayā sādhitam etayā saha
children.translated_text: What and what has been prepared by you together with her?
Show me all that -- the tempering and everything else
that has been accomplished! -- thus she addressed the mother of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Rohiṇī</s>).
On the swept kitchen platform,
arranged in rows of fresh clay vessels,
she showed the prepared temperings and other [dishes],

children.text: rādhāṃ praśaṃsanty atha tāṃ ca rohiṇī
children.translated_text: and <s>Rohiṇī</s> then praised <s>Rādhā</s>.
Exceedingly sweet, better prepared than even by the moon,
cooked soft by the skilled <s>Rādhā</s>,
well-stored in the finest churning vessels --
O beautiful-faced friend, behold before you the <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-pudding)!
Strengthening, nourishing, delightful,
sweet, soft, O virtuous one!
See the <s>saṃyāva</s> (a flour-based sweet), stored in churning vessels,
made by her!
With plantain, sugar-cane juice, and cream,
<s>śaṣkulī</s> (pastries) of many kinds, O friend!
See also the flour preparations,
of many varieties, well-prepared!
<s>Pīyūṣagranthi</s> (ambrosia-knots), <s>karpūrakelikā</s> (camphor-delights),
<s>amṛtakelikā</s> (nectar-delights) --
prepared by her, see [them] --
methods that are beyond even my knowledge!
This one, purely moistened churned [lentil],
is a <s>vaṭaka</s> (fritter) of <s>mudga</s> (mung bean), of two kinds,
with combinations of sugar and salt,
also of <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), of four kinds.
With tamarind, hog-plum, and sour mango,
through combination with the respective ingredients,
slightly sweet, strongly [flavored], and such --
the sour [preparations] are of twelve kinds.
Of tied plantain and its fresh core,
and portions of its fresh buds,
of <s>mānakanda</s> (a root vegetable), water-tuber, <s>kacvī</s> (a tuber),
of primary portions and of <s>āluka</s> (potato),
of pumpkin and <s>ḍiṇḍīśa</s> (a gourd) --
a network of disc-shaped pieces,
coated with chickpea-flour paste,
fried in ghee, each separately;
<s>vaṭaka</s> (fritters) of chickpea flour,
fried only in clarified butter,
and others, soaked in the broth of excellent
sour buttermilk -- behold!
Balls of chickpea flour,
steamed in boiling water,
pieces [of them] with various differences
in ingredients, cooking, and such --
patties of fruits and roots,
separately, with different combinations,
with the three spices (cardamom, cinnamon, clove), pepper, and such,
made into many varieties.
<s>Karkāru</s> (a gourd), <s>jyotsnikā</s>, bottle-gourd
fruits -- friend -- each separately,
with a combination of mustard and curd,
prepared by her, O auspicious one!
Flowers desired by the children,
fried only in ghee;
fried in ghee and soaked in curd --
buds of the <s>kovidāra</s> (bauhinia) tree;
fried in ghee and soaked in curd --
flower-patties of two kinds;
<s>Paṭola</s> (pointed gourd) fruits, fried
in clarified butter -- thoroughly flavor-giving!
Patties of mature pumpkin,
with <s>kacvī</s> (a tuber), <s>mānālu</s> (yam), and tubers,
enriched with ground bitter and sweet [spices],
others made rich with <s>cavikā</s> (long pepper);
Made by her from milk-[cooked] bottle-gourd,
with sugar, cardamom, and pepper combined,
and from that combination, another sweet [dish],
called <s>kṣīra-kuṣmāṇḍa</s> (milk-pumpkin);
<s>Dadhi-śūraṇaka</s> (curd-yam) -- sweet;
and <s>dhātrī-śūraṇaka</s> (amla-yam) -- excellent;
one [fried] with curd, and the other roasted --
<s>kāravilva</s> (bitter gourd) fruit, of two kinds;
Of soft plantain-core pieces
and mature pumpkin pieces,
a preparation with sugar and curd,
sweet-sour and very cooling;
<s>Nālīta</s> (jute leaves), fenugreek, <s>śatapuṣpikā</s> (dill), fennel,
<s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), <s>vāstūka</s> (chenopodium), <s>vitunna</s>, <s>māriṣa</s> (amaranth) --
by her, through differences of method and combination,
leafy greens (<s>śāka</s>) well-prepared, stealing the pride of ambrosia;
<s>Kalambī</s> (a curry) of ripe tamarind,
cooked in its juice -- flavor-bestowing;
this <s>kṛṣṇa-nālīta</s> (dark jute-leaf) curry,
excellent with unripe mango fruit;
Of <s>mayuṣṭhaka</s> (a lentil variety), mung bean,
and also black gram -- just now by me,
this threefold <s>sūpa</s> (lentil soup), resembling
a well of nectar, is being cooked;
With pastes of flower-powders,
thoroughly pressed by the maidservants,
in the shape of full-moon discs,
<s>roṭikā</s> (flatbreads) are being made by me;
Some [dishes] have been made, some are being made,
and some yet remain to be made --
thus, these rice dishes and curries,
understand [them] as fully accomplished by us two.
Seeing all that -- fragrant, of excellent color, and enchanting --
she became delighted.
Then, as she inquired about the method of preparation,
<s>Rohiṇī</s> spoke to her with wonder:
The ingredients are the same ordinary ones,
and the cooking procedure is also that [standard one];
but the cause of the unprecedented quality
is the skillful hand of the heavenly musician's [daughter] (<s>Gāndharvā</s>, i.e., <s>Rādhā</s>).
Seeing her, <s>Rādhā</s>, absorbed in food preparation,
perspiring, her face lowered in modesty,
the queen (<s>Yaśodā</s>), her heart melting with affection,
ordered her maidservant to fan her.
Then she described her serving skills:
On the dining area spread with cloth, before the auspicious jeweled seat,
rows of jeweled boxes of the respective curry-jewels in order on both sides;
rows of boxes of sweet, desired, excellent flour-preparations outside those;
rows of golden boxes of fine, excellent dairy-preparations outside those;
thus, in order, in a semicircular arrangement, in rows, wonderfully,
made variegated by the abundantly beautiful, colorful arrangement by her companions,
with mutually intertwined, subtle, fragrant, smooth drippings of ghee,

children.text: madhye hemamayī vyadhāyi rucirā pātrī śubhair odanaiḥ
children.translated_text: in the center was placed a beautiful golden vessel with auspicious rice;
a golden serving-plate, with ghee, <s>puṭī</s>-fruit, <s>limpāka</s>, sugar-pieces and such,
together with pieces of preserved, moist <s>rasāla</s> (mango), and excellent <s>kāsamarda</s> and others,

children.text: yuktāṃ dakṣiṇato nidhāya nika e tasyāś ca bhṛṅgārakān
children.translated_text: having placed it to the right, neatly, and her water-vessels

children.text: karpūreṇa suvāsitena payasā pūrṇān vyadhāt kānakān
children.translated_text: filled golden [vessels] with milk fragrant with camphor.
Seeing the manifold culinary skill of her [<s>Rādhā's</s>] cooking, the beloved of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> [<s>Yaśodā</s>],
greatly astonished at the wonderful arrangement of their serving,

children.text: ānetuṃ prajighāya vatsala-manāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ ca rāmaṃ ca sā
children.translated_text: sent with a loving heart to bring <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: dhātreyīm atha tau samīyatur atiśraddhā-vaśād añjasā
children.translated_text: Then those two came to their foster-mother with utmost devotion, straightaway;

children.text: natvā mātaram ājñayā saha-balas tasyāḥ samullāsanaḥ
children.translated_text: bowing to [their] mother, by her command, together with his brother, delighting her,
with his lotus-feet washed lovingly by the young maidservants,
having sipped water [for purification], he sat down face-to-face before the beautiful dishes of food.
Observing all that, his mind amazed, the yellow-garmented one shone forth.
<s>Śrīdāmā</s> and <s>Subala</s> on the left,
before him <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>,
<s>Śrī Bala</s> on the right, and the others
sat around [him].

children.text: mātṛbhyāṃ krama-darśitena hi pathā bhoktuṃ samārabdhavān
children.translated_text: By the method shown step by step by the two mothers, he began to eat;

children.text: yad yad bhoktum upakramaṃ sma kurute tyaktuṃ na tat soḍhavān
children.translated_text: whatever he commenced to eat, he could not bear to leave it;

children.text: bhoktuṃ tat tad aśeṣam apy abhilaṣan sāmarthyavāṃś ca svayaṃ
children.translated_text: desiring to eat each and every one completely, though capable himself,

children.text: kiñcit kiñcid abhukta vīkṣaka-bhiyā durvāda-bhītyāpy ayam
children.translated_text: he ate only a little of each, out of fear of onlookers and fear of gossip.
With his fellow-diners explaining, together with his brothers, the skill of the cooking,

children.text: svāduṅkāram adann avāg api hṛdā so 'pi praśaṃsann alam
children.translated_text: making sounds of relish, eating, though silent, praising abundantly in his heart,
first he ate some <s>pāyasa</s> (sweet rice pudding), then seeing the sufficiency of other abundant [dishes],
with greed directed by the effort toward the jewel-like side dishes, amassed in plenty,
in order, beginning with vegetables, out of satisfaction, all the excellent side-dishes

children.text: ny ādan mātṛ-mude bhaved api yathā paktrī-manorañjanā
children.translated_text: he ate, so that the cook might be delighted, for his mother's joy.

children.text: tān sarvān saha-bhojinaḥ sarasayā vācā hasan hāsayan
children.translated_text: Making all those fellow-diners laugh with witty words, laughing and causing laughter,

children.text: bhuñjadhvaṃ na parityajeta kim apīty ekāntam āhlādayan
children.translated_text: 'Eat! Do not leave anything!' — thus he thoroughly delighted them.
The sweet foods prepared by each [<s>gopī</s>] individually,
suitable for the morning meal —
those <s>gopīs</s>, summoned by her [<s>Yaśodā</s>], joyfully
brought and presented to the mother.
The <s>laḍḍukas</s> (sweet balls) made of sugar-candy,
brought with effort from her home by <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> —
those, called '<s>Gaṅgā-jala</s>' (Ganges water), <s>Raṅgadevī</s>
offered to the mother by [<s>Rādhā's</s>] gesture.
The mother, dividing those lovingly
for <s>Bala</s> and the others, gave [them],
placing them separately
in scattered golden plates.
Savoring the food cooked in ghee,
making them laugh with witty jests,
glancing with the corner of his eye
at <s>Rādhā's</s> face — the friends saw him with delight.
'That is excellent, this is sweet,
this is rich, that is beautiful' —
the mother, pointing with her finger,
said, 'Eat, dear child!'
Whatever was desired by whomever,
knowing and knowing [each one's wish], laughing, <s>Hari</s>
gave that and that to this one and that one,
