repeatedly tossing [food] from his own plate.
Seeing the mother attentive with effort
and <s>Acyuta</s> eating slowly,
the <s>baṭu</s> (young brāhmaṇa student) [<s>Madhumaṅgala</s>], clever in jest,
said to the queen of <s>Vraja</s>:
'If this one doesn't eat much, O mother!
Give it all to me — I'll eat it all!
Embraced by me, he'll become plump
thanks to me, the great eater.'
'This one of feeble appetite has no capacity
for eating food cooked in ghee;
so, O mother, have light-cooked food
and side-dishes given to him!'
Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, laughing, with handfuls
of cooked food from his own plate,
filled the <s>baṭu's</s> vessel
with five or six [handfuls], saying 'Eat!'
Then, slapping his own left elbow
on his left side,
having begun to eat properly,
the delighted <s>baṭu</s> said to him:
'Friend! Watch me eat!'
— thus eating two mouthfuls [at once],
'Mother, give me yogurt!' —
he sent her to fetch it then.
'Cowherds, look! A restless one is dancing here, having found his heart's desire in cooked food —

children.text: kīśeśo dadhi-lampa o 'yam iti tān kṛtvonmukhāṃs tad-diśi
children.translated_text: this monkey-lord is a yogurt-glutton!' — thus turning them toward that direction,

children.text: teṣāṃ bhojana-bhājaneṣu śanakair nikṣipya bhakṣyaṃ nijaṃ
children.translated_text: he quietly placed his own food into their eating-vessels,

children.text: sarvaṃ bhuktam idaṃ mayeti sa punar garvāyamāno 'vadat
children.translated_text: and then, boasting, said: 'I've eaten all of this!'
When she came back with the yogurt-vessel in hand,
he said: 'Look, mother! Even without the yogurt,
I have quickly eaten everything!
So give me a great deal of <s>pāyasa</s> (sweet rice pudding)!'
The <s>pāyasa</s>, placed in golden vessels by <s>Rādhā</s>,
cooled by gentle breezes from fresh banana leaves,
served into their hands,
<s>Rohiṇī</s> quickly gave to them.
Bringing again and again the side-dishes
prepared by <s>Gāndharvā</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>],
vegetables and other [dishes], ending with sour [items],
she gave to them gradually and slowly.
Light in color and texture, [made] on banana-leaf bases,
fine wheat-flour <s>roṭikās</s> (flatbreads), well-ground,
anointed with ghee, served by her,
she placed in separate vessels and gave to them.
Previously regarding the cooked food,
and now regarding the rice and other [dishes],
the <s>baṭu's</s> fine jesting words —
there would be no repetition here.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> ate eagerly, not [getting enough] here;
<s>Bala</s> ate only a morsel;
<s>Śrīdāmā</s> by name was a slow eater;
<s>Subala</s> was as if bereft of strength.
'Where is their lack of single-minded devotion
to food — [it is mere] lack of sophistication!
And where is this food that puts nectar to shame,
prepared by <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself!
Does not even poetry composed by a great poet
go to waste
where in the assembly there is no
eagerness to savor it?'
'This four-fold food is the <s>catur-varga</s> (four aims of life) in embodied form;
I alone am the sole
worthy recipient of it' —
said the <s>baṭu</s>.
<s>Śrīdāmā</s> said: 'Fill your belly
quickly with [these] balls of food!
That alone is your everything,
that for which you assumed the student's role.'
The <s>baṭu</s> retorted: 'Hey, fool!
You are a cowherd — what would you understand?
For savoring flavors, for the sake of one's <s>dharma</s>,
go roam the forest to pen the cows!'
'Behold! I am a learned one,
a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, into whose mouth [offerings are] poured!
By those [offerings], the Lord alone
is worshipped through all sacrifices.'
<s>Śrīdāmā</s> said: 'Even the path of <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>,
in a hundred lifetimes,
you have never studied;
your brāhmaṇahood is just the sacred thread!'
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'The <s>baṭu</s> has
training in the science of flavors,
since he has expertise in recognizing
the characteristics and meaning of various side-dishes.'
The <s>baṭu</s> said: 'There are only six
flavors here, not eight, in my opinion;
tasting is proper in only six ways,
since we have only six sense-organs.'
'Those who say there are eight flavors —
they too depend on side-dishes;
but not even a trace of expertise
in side-dishes exists in them.'
'Leaving aside vegetables, soups, and the like,
abandoning them, they suck up
that water — clearly leaving aside [the substance],
they chase after a mirage!'
'The cause of the production of <s>rasa</s> (flavor),
they said, is chewing;
but they are dried up by chewing —
not even in ten million lifetimes of [their] father [would they understand]!'
<s>Rāma</s> said: 'In the savoring of flavors,
what are the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent effects) in your view?
And what are the <s>sañcāriṇas</s> (transitory emotions)? What is
the <s>sthāyī</s> (permanent emotion)? How is it savored?'
The <s>baṭu</s> said: 'That which, from non-attainment [of food],
first produces my tears;
but upon attaining this side-dish,
[produces] horripilation and facial delight;'
'From the satisfaction of the richness of its color,
[comes] pallor — see that in me!
When I speak while eating,
my voice is thereby broken;'
'My paralysis is born from the grief of inability
to eat abundant sweet food;
perspiration is evident, and at the end,
dissolution [comes] from excessive eating;'
'Laziness, contemplation, drowsiness, and the like —
these are clearly our transitory emotions here;
the permanent emotion, though one in its nature as savorability,
has various names.'
'The rice cooked in ghee,
I consider [it to be] as if bathed
in golden water — the fragrance
of which has attained accessibility.'
'In a cowherd assembly that smells of grass
cut by cow's teeth,
for me, one of accumulated merit, by association
a partaker of great enjoyment —'
'In the forest, <s>brāhmaṇas</s> perform austerities,
eating leaves, roots, and fruits;
O <s>baṭu</s>! You have no right to enjoyment —
go, practice austerities!'
'True indeed! Those who formerly performed austerities
with leaves, roots, fruits, and the like —
maturing in this birth,
they have become side-dishes for me!'
'The heavenly fruits of those dwelling on earth
are well perceived directly day after day;
thus know that this [fruit of] enjoyment
comes not to those who have not performed austerities.'
'If so, then these wrinkle-faced ones [monkeys]
deserve to receive [these foods] first;
even in [their] labors of verbal expenditure,
these in [their] births are ascetics —'
'bearing cold, heat, and wind,
eating leaves, flowers, and fruits;
being possessed of memory of past lives, how could they not be?
Who knows the wisdom of these [monkeys]?'
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Friend! <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>
are devoted to the worship of <s>Brahman</s>;
monkeys are mere belly-fillers —
between these two there is a great difference.'
'And I perceive no difference
between this monkey [and you], O <s>Hari</s>!
Humanness or monkeyness —
between these two there is no cause for distinction.'
'Moreover, proclaiming in the world
his own unprecedented wisdom,
because of its greatness and its capacity to nourish,
he considers his own belly to be <s>Brahman</s>.'
'Therefore, meditating three times a day
on the means of its fulfillment,
that [belly] alone is worshipped by him,
this lifelong <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student)!'
'Sometimes, by the frenzy and commotion
of devouring abundantly cooked food,
monkey-like behavior would occur, with the nimbleness
of his hands while eating.'
Having said this, he made everyone laugh —
<s>Subala</s>, and the <s>baṭu</s> too,
laughing while still eating, loudly,
became red-faced from coughing.
The lord of the cowherd settlement said: '<s>Baṭu</s>! Stop!
For a moment, don't eat, don't laugh!
Be still, don't prattle —
and you boys, don't make him laugh!'
The various [foods] — <s>rasāla</s> (mango preparations) and the like — prepared by <s>Lalitā</s> and others,
brought before [them] by <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>,
the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, placing them separately in rows of vessels,
distributed them lovingly to these [boys] and rejoiced.
Delighted by the sight of their heart's beloved's face,
drawn by his extremely sweet, soft beauty,
they rejoiced, overcome with arising expansive emotions,
those praiseworthy ones, in the beloved's house.
Then, those four kinds of food,
as if transformations born of the essence of nectar,
savoring the sweet [foods] with eagerness,
making him laugh with jests, they laughed.
Some chew the chewable soft foods;
others restlessly lick the lickable ones;
others, delighted, drink the drinkable ones;
still others, satisfied, suck the suckable ones.

children.text: svāduṅkāraṃ kamala-nayanaḥ saspṛhaṃ tat tad annaṃ
children.translated_text: The lotus-eyed one, making sounds of relish, eagerly, each food,
made nectar-sweet by the hand-touch of his beloved, slowly and gently,
his eye-corner bees sent to her lotus-face — secretly

children.text: prāśnann ambā-manasi nibiḍaṃ sa pramodaṃ vyatānīt
children.translated_text: eating, he spread dense delight in his mother's heart.
With the channel of glances from the corners of her startled, darting eyes
meeting his, nourished by tasting the nectar of his surpassing beauty,
concealing the delight of all her arising emotions,
<s>Rādhikā</s> too stole her beloved's heart.
Then, placing the mother of <s>Bala</s> [<s>Rohiṇī</s>] between [herself and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], dancing,
the intoxicated, wine-eyed one [<s>Rādhā</s>], offering into her [<s>Rohiṇī's</s>] hand

children.text: mṛdu mṛdu madhurānnaṃ preyasīṃ prekṣya kṛṣṇaḥ
children.translated_text: the soft, sweet food — when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> saw his beloved,
the lord of the sophisticated lost his appetite for food and became absent-minded.
He had eaten only partially,
with some one-third remaining;
seeing the uneaten food and his slow eating,
the mother became anxious.
'All the food and other [dishes] carefully prepared —
how have you abandoned them all, O son!
You are hungry — eat some more!
I swear on your head!'
'Having brought the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> with effort,
all this food was prepared by that daughter-in-law,
sweet beyond the value of nectar —
yet you do not eat! What shall I, wretched, do?'
Then she said to <s>Rohiṇī</s>:
'Look, <s>Rohiṇī</s>! The restless one,
though weak and hungry,
this slow eater eats hardly anything!'
Then, her body pervaded with affection,
caressing the crusher of <s>Agha</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>],
this mother of the slayer of <s>Pralamba</s> [<s>Balarāma</s>],
standing before him, said:
'The food was prepared with effort, dear child, and is sweet,
by the gentle <s>Mallī</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>] and by me —

children.text: kṣut-kṣāmo 'si tvaṃ ca nāśnāsi tat tām
children.translated_text: you are emaciated with hunger, yet you do not eat;

children.text: ambām etāṃ māṃ ca kiṃvā dunoṣi
children.translated_text: why then do you torment this mother and me?'
'Look, your mother is distressed,
O son! I shall perform the averting-of-evil rite for you;
there will be fatigue from wandering in the forest —
eat some more, heed my words!'
'I have eaten much, my hunger is gone' —
saying thus, suppressing the rising emotion,

children.text: taṃ vīkṣya mandaṃ punar apy adantaṃ
children.translated_text: seeing him eat slowly again,
the two mothers rejoiced over the son of <s>Nanda</s>.

children.text: idam idam atimiṣṭaṃ vatsa! bhuṅkṣveti mātā
children.translated_text: 'This, this is most delicious, child! Eat!' — thus the mother,
with oaths, pointing to this and that with her fingers,
wishing to accomplish everything, her eyes flooded with tears,
says that the food has entered the belly along with her son.
Mango juice, ripe mangoes, liquid <s>śikhariṇī</s> (sweet curd preparation), <s>ṣāḍava</s> (sweet dish), milk,
<s>karambha</s> (porridge), sour gruel, side-dishes, yogurt, fruits, cakes, and <s>vaṭaka</s> (fried balls) —
repeatedly urging, her cloth moistened with the milk of her tear-streaming breasts,

children.text: py atṛptā taṃ tṛptaṃ muhur atha sutaṃ prāśayad iyam
children.translated_text: yet unsatisfied, she fed her satisfied son again and again.
Foods to be chewed, foods to be swallowed, most abundant sweets,
foods to be licked, drinks, soft and sweet for you —
having eaten and drunk, satiated with the fullness of flavors,
all became eager to go to the forest.
All of them, having well wiped their lotus-hands and mouths

children.text: ny āmṛjya sādhu mṛduleṣikayā ca dantān
children.translated_text: with fragrant, soft earth, and their teeth with a soft brush,
in golden and other vessels brought by servants,
they performed <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping of water) with water given by them.
With <s>elā</s> (cardamom), <s>lavaṅga</s> (clove), and camphor-mixed
excellent <s>khādira</s> (catechu) balls given with <s>jambūla</s> (rose-apple),
cool and radiant, having perfumed their mouths with delight,
they rubbed their full bellies with the left hand.
Betel-rolls made of well-ripened, gleaming <s>nāgavallī</s> (betel) leaves,
skillfully prepared — they chewed them eagerly and happily.
Then, upon the spacious couches arranged at intervals of a hundred steps,

children.text: kuleṣv atha viśaśramuḥ parijanair amī vījitāḥ
children.translated_text: they reclined to rest, fanned by attendants.
As he rested there, the attendants
fanned him with peacock-feather fans.
Breaking a leaf [of betel] into soft rolls,
a playful attendant offered them to the lord.
Emerging from the kitchen with washed feet and hands,
attended by groups of maidservants with fans,
<s>Rādhā</s>, who had come to the inner chamber, with her companion-women,
gazing at her beloved through the lattice-window —
perspiring with the drops of joy-born sweat,
she was recognized by the queen of <s>Vraja</s> as merely exhausted from exertion.
Seating her with effort to eat, she [<s>Yaśodā</s>] joyfully
had food brought forcefully from the house of <s>Balabhadra's</s> mother.
Instructed by her, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, to give
ghee-prepared food mixed secretly
with the remnants of <s>Hari's</s> meal,
brought it from the house at that time and gave it to them.
Seeing [<s>Rādhā</s>] not eating, out of shyness,
her face lowered and covered with her garment,
<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> mother spoke to <s>Rādhikā</s>,
overcome with maternal affection:

children.text: janani! mayi jananyāṃ kiṃ nu lajjedṛśīyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'O daughter! Before me, your mother, why such shyness?

children.text: suta iva mama cetaḥ snihyati tvayy atīva
children.translated_text: My heart loves you exceedingly, as [it loves] my own son.

children.text: ayi tad apanayaināṃ yāmi nirmañcanaṃ te
children.translated_text: Come, set aside this [shyness] — I shall go to perform your <s>nirmañcana</s> (protective rite).

children.text: śiśiraya mama netraṃ bhuṅkṣva paśyāmi sākṣāt
children.translated_text: Cool my eyes — eat! Let me see directly.'

children.text: yūyaṃ ca me stha tanayās tv anayā hriyā kiṃ
children.translated_text: 'All of you are also my daughters — so why this shyness?
O <s>Lalitā</s> and others, eat your food!'
Thus, with insistence and hundreds of affectionate oaths,
the mother fed them with sweet foods and sweet words.
Then, with their own pairs of lotus-hands washed by maidservants,
these [ladies], having rinsed their own faces with water mixed with moonbeams [camphor],

children.text: pa air mārjitvā ca svaparijana-dattā himakarā
children.translated_text: having wiped with cloths and received from their attendants the cool [betel],

children.text: viyuktā vī īs tā vara-kanaka-gauryo bubhujire
children.translated_text: separated from the betel-rolls — those beautiful ones of golden complexion enjoyed them.
With desires arising in her heart to take her son's hand [in marriage for them],

children.text: tad bhūṣaṇaiḥ subahuśaḥ saha yāni yatnāt
children.translated_text: those ornaments, together with which, with great effort,
having fashioned replicas [suitable] for new brides,
were kept with affection in the house in fine jewel-caskets.
With those ornaments then brought by <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>,
along with betel, sandalwood, fresh garments, and <s>nāgaja</s> (camphor),
honoring her, surrounded by companions, as if a new bride —
the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, her heart overflowing, became joyful.
The garment that <s>Rādhā</s> had taken at night — <s>Viśākhā</s>
gave it secretly to <s>Subala</s> through <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>.
And <s>Subala</s> [gave] to her [<s>Rādhā</s>]
the blue garment taken by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — the yellow upper-cloth [in exchange] — through her [<s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>] alone.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the second collection, called 'The Collection of Morning Pastimes,' in the blessed <s>Bhāvanā-sāra-saṅgraha</s>.
